set.verdict: Traders With Edge once advertised Hong Kong-linked simulated evaluation products, but its former official domain could not be reached during this review. Earlier PropRadar access returned only a private account/login page, and independent October 2026 checks also reported a nonfunctioning site. Current checkout, operator, enforceable contract and payouts cannot be verified. Some current-looking third-party directories copy historical terms and incorrectly label it active without demonstrating a working company storefront. PropRadar lowers the historical 40/100 to 22 and blocks challenge purchases. Commercial inactivity is suspected, but neither a formal closure announcement nor legal dissolution has been established.
set.auditSummary: 17 November 2026: the previously advertised traderswithedge.com domain timed out in a fresh public-page attempt. PropRadar's July capture had already found an account-only screen rather than a public prop-firm offer; independent dated checks reported DNS/homepage failures in 2026. The archived historical program figures, reported payout claims and static review pages are not evidence of a current operating service. No first-party announcement of a lawful migration, verified new domain, working checkout, contracting entity, refund policy, open funded account support or current profit withdrawals could be authenticated. A current Crunchbase listing describing the company as 'Active' is a business-directory status, not proof of a live commercial storefront. Until a functioning primary source and legal counterparty are found, any new offer under this name or old domain has high impersonation and payment risk. Score 40 to 22; no claim of proven liquidation, and checkout links are disabled.

restrictiveRules.rule: Max Risk Rule: if combined floating loss on open positions reaches 1.5% of the initial balance at any moment, the Instant account is breached and terminated on the first violation (accounts bought after 31 Aug 2026); per-size lot caps also apply on forex pairs and gold.
restrictiveRules.impact: A temporary floating loss of 1.5% ends the account even if the trade later recovers.

restrictiveRules.rule: 1% floating loss rule: the first trigger closes positions and reduces the profit split to 30%; the second trigger breaches and permanently closes the account.
restrictiveRules.impact: One trigger cuts the trader's share to 30%; a second ends the account.

restrictiveRules.rule: Max floating risk 1.5% of the initial balance: first breach is a soft breach that reduces the profit split to 40%; second breach is a hard breach and the account is terminated. Per-size lot caps apply on forex pairs and gold on the funded stage.
restrictiveRules.impact: A first breach cuts the trader's share to 40%; a second ends the funded account.

restrictiveRules.program: Instant Lite, Instant Flex, 2-Step Lite - funded stage
restrictiveRules.rule: Daily profit limit of $3,000 per trading day on all funded account sizes; 'any profit exceeding the daily limit will be deducted from the account upon review' (not a breach). Instant Flex also caps each payout at 4%.
restrictiveRules.impact: Profit above $3,000 on a single day is removed rather than paid.

restrictiveRules.rule: Funded accounts bought after 21 Oct 2026 must hold every trade at least 60 seconds (2 minutes for older accounts) unless a paid add-on is bought; a confirmed violation leads to account termination and payout rejection.
restrictiveRules.impact: Trades closed under 60 seconds can cost the payout and the funded account.

restrictiveRules.rule: No new trades 5 minutes before/after news (Instant Lite) or 4 minutes before/after (challenge funded accounts); a trade opened in the window means the payout is rejected, and profit from earlier trades closed during news is removed on review.
restrictiveRules.impact: News-window trades lead to a rejected payout or removed profit.

restrictiveRules.rule: On Instant Flex, a news trading violation on the funded account without the news add-on is a hard breach.
restrictiveRules.impact: A news-window trade closes the account.

restrictiveRules.rule: VPN and VPS use is not allowed and 'may result in an account violation'; confirmed violations lead to termination and payout rejection.
restrictiveRules.impact: Trading through a VPN or VPS can end the account and cancel the payout.

restrictiveRules.rule: Payout name must match the account name and the payout address must not be used on another FundedSquad account; sharing a crypto wallet with another user means 'your payout will be rejected and your account permanently banned'. Payouts can only be requested on weekdays.
restrictiveRules.impact: A shared wallet address cancels the payout and closes the account.

restrictiveRules.rule: No trading activity for 21 consecutive calendar days breaches the account, counted from the purchase date.
restrictiveRules.impact: An unused account is closed after 21 days.

restrictiveRules.rule: Instant accounts must close all positions before the weekend unless the Weekend Holding add-on is bought.
restrictiveRules.impact: Constrains holding trades over the weekend.

restrictiveRules.rule: Terms of Service section 4.6: 'The Company reserves the right to disallow or block any Trader from participating in the program at its sole discretion.'
restrictiveRules.impact: Participation, and therefore payouts, can be stopped without a stated rule breach.

restrictiveRules.rule: The first payout requires five winning days of at least 0.2% each and the EOD drawdown floor to lock after a balance of $52,100/$103,100/$154,600, depending on the $50K/$100K/$150K size. Only 50% of the gains above that locked level can then be requested, subject to a separate payout cap.
restrictiveRules.impact: The headline 90% profit split is not a promise that all profits are immediately withdrawable; the lock, winning-day threshold and first cap must be reached.

restrictiveRules.rule: Five winning days of at least 0.2% each and the drawdown safety buffer are prerequisites. The best winning day must stay within 30% of cumulative cycle profits; progressive per-request caps start at $1,500/$2,000/$2,500 depending on size.
restrictiveRules.impact: Profitable trading may continue before a reward is eligible; the payout cap is independent of the advertised 90% share.

restrictiveRules.rule: The first reward is unlocked only after $3,000/$6,000/$9,000 of new profit by size; later cycles need fresh profit and have their own targets. The best day must represent less than 20% of current-cycle profit, with progressive payout caps.
restrictiveRules.impact: There is no minimum-day count, but a sizable profit trigger and a strict best-day ratio delay access to withdrawals.

restrictiveRules.rule: Gambling includes 'any position whose potential loss equals all, or nearly all, of the account's drawdown' and abusive DCA; 'The final assessment of whether a practice falls within this Article rests with MILTRADERS'. Under article 12.5 the requested payout is reviewed and may be approved or declined at MilTraders' discretion, funded accounts are closed, started evaluations and funded accounts are not refunded, and a permanent ban follows. The FAQ instead says 'MILTRADERS honors the payout currently requested'.
restrictiveRules.impact: Under the terms a pending payout can be refused on the firm's own reading of a qualitative test, while the FAQ promises it is honoured; the official documents disagree.

restrictiveRules.rule: A change to the Program Rules 'applies to all accounts, including accounts purchased before the change'; amendments to the terms apply to all accounts including earlier purchases, and the current terms replace earlier agreements for every account 'whatever its date of purchase'. Continued use means acceptance.
restrictiveRules.impact: Payout caps, consistency or other conditions can change on an account already bought.

restrictiveRules.program: Zero, Pro and Instant — compulsory live selection (terms 10.1-10.3)
restrictiveRules.rule: Selection for Live is at MilTraders' 'sole discretion' and 'A selected Trader may not decline the selection'; it requires at least one payout on the funded account. On selection 'all your simulated Accounts are blocked and can no longer be traded'; unpaid funded accounts are closed with their evaluation fees refunded, except that no refund is due if the broker refuses KYC/AML (10.9). The FAQ describes the live account as something MilTraders 'may offer to selected funded traders'.
restrictiveRules.impact: After a first payout the firm can end every simulated account at its discretion; the FAQ presents this as an offer, while the terms make it compulsory.

restrictiveRules.rule: On Live accounts the split is 80% to the trader and 20% to MilTraders for the first three payouts per account, then 90/10. The FAQ states a 90% split and does not mention the 80% phase.
restrictiveRules.impact: A trader moved to live earns a lower share on the first three live payouts than the advertised 90%.

restrictiveRules.rule: Micro-scalping is a soft breach: 'the profits from trades held under 10 seconds may be deducted' after a risk review; the account stays active.
restrictiveRules.impact: Profits from trades closed in under 10 seconds can be removed before a payout.

restrictiveRules.program: All programmes — VPN, proxy and unusual connections (terms 4.3-4.5)
restrictiveRules.rule: VPNs are allowed 'at your own risk' but not to hide location. Where 'our systems flag a connection as a VPN, proxy, hosting or otherwise unusual address', documents may be requested and 'Any pending Payout may be suspended until the review is complete'; unresolved eligibility or VPN issues allow account closure and cancellation of unpaid profits.
restrictiveRules.impact: An automated VPN or hosting flag can freeze a payout and, if the review is not resolved, cost the unpaid profits.

restrictiveRules.program: All programmes — one profile per address (terms 4.1, 4.5)
restrictiveRules.rule: Users 'hold only one user profile' and 'several persons living at the same address may not each hold their own profile'; operating multiple identities leads to a permanent ban. The FAQ caps funded accounts at 'Up to 6 funded accounts total (all types combined)'.
restrictiveRules.impact: Two traders sharing an address cannot each have a profile; a breach ends access.

restrictiveRules.rule: '30 consecutive calendar days without any trade → automatic account closure and forfeiture of unrealized profits.' Terms 8.4 allows asking support for an exception before day 30, at MilTraders' discretion.
restrictiveRules.impact: A funded account left untraded for 30 days closes and loses its unpaid profit.

restrictiveRules.rule: Residents, citizens or persons with branch operations in restricted countries are excluded; for some countries 'Eligibility in those cases is decided case by case'. Failed Rise identity verification allows refusal of activation and payouts and closure of accounts; if the live broker refuses KYC/AML, funded accounts close and 'no refund of any kind is due'.
restrictiveRules.impact: Eligibility can be decided case by case and checked late (at first payout or at the live move), with profits and fees at stake.

restrictiveRules.program: All programmes — automation and copy trading
restrictiveRules.rule: Hard breaches include 'use of bots or automated systems' and 'copying another trader's trades (verified)': 'Account is closed and all profits forfeited, with no warnings.' Terms 11.1 allow copying one's own manually placed trades between one's own accounts.
restrictiveRules.impact: Any automated order placement, including EAs, ends the account and its profits.

restrictiveRules.rule: On Zero funded accounts, positions are prohibited during the restricted window around high-impact announcements set in the Program Rules; 'profits generated by trades held inside the restricted window are removed', and repeated violations may lead to closure and a permanent ban. News trading is otherwise permitted on all programmes.
restrictiveRules.impact: Profits made during the news window on a Zero funded account are removed from the payout.

restrictiveRules.rule: For hedging (defined by product group across accounts), 'all profits made on that trading day are cancelled on every account involved' on a first violation; terms 12.2 then escalate repeated violations.
restrictiveRules.impact: A hedge between two of one's accounts cancels the whole day's profit on each of them.

set.auditSummary: 18 November 2026 desk audit of MilTraders' Zero, Pro and Instant futures programs using the firm's current FAQ and contractual terms. Zero and Pro require five sufficiently profitable days plus a locked EOD drawdown buffer; Zero permits withdrawal of only half of gains above the lock, whereas Pro adds a 30% funded best-day ratio. Instant has a sizable first-profit trigger and a 20% best-day ratio instead of a day count. Each tier has separate minimum and per-request caps, despite the advertised 90% payout split. restrictiveRules.rule: Terms section 22.4: 'Payouts remain entirely discretionary and subject to internal compliance review', and 'The Company's decision to refuse a payout based on trading style or behavior is final, binding, and non-appealable.' Section 22.3 lets the firm approve or reject accounts 'at their sole discretion' after reviewing for 'automation, or system abuse'.

restrictiveRules.program: Apex EOD and Intraday Trailing — evaluations
restrictiveRules.rule: EOD model computes the trailing floor at the day close; Intraday model adjusts its high-water floor on unrealized equity in real time. Evaluation has no minimum trading days or consistency ratio.
restrictiveRules.impact: A high intraday unrealized gain is more dangerous on Intraday than EOD; these models must not share one generic label.

restrictiveRules.rule: Five separate days must reach a size-dependent minimum profit; no single day may reach 50% of all profit since the last approved payout. Keep a Safety Net equal to drawdown plus $100 and request at least $500.
restrictiveRules.impact: A profitable PA may be unable to withdraw until multiple daily-profit, concentration and protected-balance criteria all hold.

restrictiveRules.program: Apex EOD and Intraday Performance Accounts — lifetime
restrictiveRules.rule: Each PA receives at most six sequential payouts, each capped according to size and payment sequence; after the sixth approved payout the PA is closed.
restrictiveRules.impact: Apex funded sim status is not indefinite; future withdrawals require a newly qualified account.

restrictiveRules.rule: The User Agreement states Rewards 'are discretionary and do not represent a legal asset, entitlement, or obligation of the Company', 'may be withheld, forfeited, or rescinded at any time in the Company's sole discretion', and that Apex may 'deny, modify, reduce, cap, delay, or revoke Reward distributions for any reason or no reason'. Determinations are 'final and binding' and 'not subject to appeal or review'. §11 lists penalties applied 'at its sole discretion' for any breach, including loss of unpaid Rewards, repayment of distributed Rewards, removal of profits and deletion of trading days. §30 says changes to the Agreement, Trading Rules or Reward policies take effect upon posting.
restrictiveRules.impact: Meeting the published payout criteria does not create a contractual right to a payout under the agreement's own wording; Apex keeps a stated right to refuse, reduce or claw back Rewards, and rules can change for open accounts.

restrictiveRules.program: Apex Performance Accounts — graduation and professional-proficiency termination (User Agreement §14-§15)
restrictiveRules.rule: Apex may terminate Trading Accounts if it determines 'in its sole discretion' that a user's 'trading activity, strategies, or demonstrated level of sophistication materially exceeds the level contemplated', with indicators including 'consistently exceptional performance'; it may then 'deny or revoke any unpaid Rewards'. Under 'Graduation', the Company may also remove a user at any time and decide 'at it's sole discretion' whether any final distribution is paid. Users in the Affiliate Business Development Program may be exempted.
restrictiveRules.impact: Strong, consistent performance can itself be a stated ground for account termination and loss of unpaid Rewards; no objective threshold is published.

restrictiveRules.program: Apex Performance Accounts — dormant account policy (User Agreement §16)
restrictiveRules.rule: A Performance Account is deemed dormant unless it has at least two trading days per rolling 30-day cycle with at least $50 profit on each of those days. Apex may deactivate or permanently terminate dormant PAs without notice, and 'any Rewards associated with the Performance Account(s) will be permanently forfeited regardless of prior performance or qualification status', including lifetime/one-time-payment plans.
restrictiveRules.impact: Keeping a PA open requires two profitable days (not just trading days) every 30 days; a PA that misses this can be closed and its unpaid Rewards lost.

restrictiveRules.program: Apex Evaluation and Performance Accounts — account and resource sharing
restrictiveRules.rule: 'Sharing MAC addresses, computers, IPs, credit cards, or trade copying with other traders is strictly forbidden. Violations will result in account closure, forfeiture of funds'. VPNs, proxy servers, cloud servers or anonymizing tools may not be used to misrepresent identity, device or location to circumvent rules or geographic restrictions.
restrictiveRules.impact: Trading from a shared computer or IP (for example in a household or office) can lead to closure and forfeiture under this clause.

restrictiveRules.program: Apex Evaluation and Performance Accounts — positions closed by 4:59 PM ET
restrictiveRules.rule: All positions must be closed by 4:59:00 PM ET; 'any positions that are open at 5:00:00 PM ET may result in a failed and terminated Trading Account'. The Prohibited Activities page adds that traders holding through the market close 'will forfeit their accounts and all associated balances'.
restrictiveRules.impact: Holding a position past the daily close is not just a constraint: the stated consequence is account termination and loss of balance.

restrictiveRules.program: Apex Evaluation and Performance Accounts — no automation (User Agreement)
restrictiveRules.rule: Automated execution, pre-configured bots, scripts or strategies that place, modify or cancel orders are prohibited (signal/alert tools that do not place orders are allowed). Violations 'may result in immediate termination of the User's account and forfeiture of any pending or unpaid Rewards, at the Company's sole discretion'. HFT and non-directional bracket orders around price are also listed as prohibited.
restrictiveRules.impact: Any order-placing automation can cost pending Rewards, not only the account.

restrictiveRules.program: Apex Evaluation and Performance Accounts — risk-management standards
restrictiveRules.rule: All trades must have 'pending or mental stop losses'; strategies with small targets and disproportionately large risk are banned (example: 5-tick target with 150-tick stop); using the trailing threshold as a stop loss is prohibited; any trading that 'fails to demonstrate consistent growth and sustainability' or deviates from what the trader 'would use in a personally funded account' is prohibited. Failure 'may result in placement in Trader Probation'.
restrictiveRules.impact: Several of these standards ('unsustainable', 'professional standards') are not defined numerically, so whether a strategy complies is decided by Apex after the fact.

restrictiveRules.program: Apex Evaluation and Performance Accounts — news and hedging
restrictiveRules.rule: Trading during news is allowed for a normal strategy, but 'news trading strategies that chase the market or place orders on both sides' to 'gamble the outcome of news' are not allowed. Holding long and short positions on the same or correlated instruments simultaneously is 'strictly prohibited'.
restrictiveRules.impact: News trading is permitted in principle; the boundary with a prohibited news strategy is left to Apex's judgment.

restrictiveRules.program: Apex Performance Accounts — payment method in own name
restrictiveRules.rule: Fees must be paid with a card or bank account in the user's own name and Rewards go only to a bank account in the user's own name. set.verdict: Blue Guardian sells genuinely different 2026 challenge and instant models. Most one-step/instant CFDs trail closed balance, whereas 2-Step Standard and Nano are static. Published anti-tick-scalping terms require a two-minute trade hold on relevant CFD offers; the FAQ reviewed does not specify an SL/TP exception, so PropRadar does not assume one. Instant Standard Guardian Shield triggers at 1% combined floating loss: first trigger permanently cuts profit split to 50%, second closes the account. These especially restrictive conditions lower the editorial score from 66 to 62/100.
set.auditSummary: 18 November 2026: the Blue Guardian help center was updated 13-17 November 2026 with separate CFD plan articles. 1-Step Standard: 9% target, 4% daily, 6% trailing high-closed-balance max locking after +6%, 3 profitable 0.5% days and funded Guardian Shield at 2% floating loss. 2-Step Standard: 8%+4% target, 4% daily and 8% static max, same three days per evaluation phase. 2-Step Nano: 10% static and 3% daily with 50% funded best-day/2% payout cap. Instant Standard: 3% daily and 6% trailing max, 5 profitable 0.5% days, 20% best-day funded ratio (15% for 300K/400K), a 1% funded combined floating-loss Shield where first trigger permanently reduces split to 50% and second is hard account breach; a 1% buffer after drawdown lock. Instant Starter: 5% trailing on a $5K one-off with capped crypto payout. Specific CFD articles state a minimum two-minute holding period; no published SL/TP exception verified. Futures Express stopped being sold 16 November and is not marketed as current. Score 66 to 62 for transparently published but severe risk/withdrawal controls.

restrictiveRules.program: 1 Step Standard, 2 Step Standard and Instant Starter — funded Guardian Shield
restrictiveRules.rule: "If your open trades reach a combined 2% floating loss, Guardian Shield will usually close all open trades" (1 Step and 2 Step Standard funded; 1% / $50 on Instant Starter). A first trigger cuts the profit split to 50% permanently; a second permanently breaches the account.
restrictiveRules.impact: A combined floating loss of 2% (1% on Instant Starter) closes trades, halves the profit split for the rest of the account's life on the first occurrence and ends the account on the second.

restrictiveRules.program: All CFD plans — margin use ("all or nothing" gambling)
restrictiveRules.rule: Prohibited trading strategies article (CFD): "Using more than 80% of your margin on open trades counts as 'all or nothing' gambling"; consequences include payout rejection, profit removal or termination. The Terms add that Blue Guardian may refuse a withdrawal or terminate if it deems the customer "abused margin availability".
restrictiveRules.impact: Using more than 80% of available margin at once can lead to profits removed, a payout refused or the account closed.

restrictiveRules.program: Funded accounts from 1 Step, 2 Step, 2 Step Nano evaluations and Instant Standard — news
restrictiveRules.rule: CFD news trading rules: no opening or closing trades on affected instruments from 5 minutes before to 5 minutes after high-impact news, and FOMC events of any impact. "Profit made in that window, or heavily driven by the news, will be removed, but your account won't be breached." Evaluations and Instant Starter are not restricted.
restrictiveRules.impact: Profit from trades in the window is removed; profit judged "heavily driven by the news" outside it can also be removed, a criterion the article does not define.

restrictiveRules.program: All plans — devices (CID) and account sharing
restrictiveRules.rule: Account rules article: "you must not log in to your account from a device that has been used to log in to another trader's account", including devices of friends, family, colleagues, trading communities, "shared computers and VPS services". A device-ID (CID) match means accounts "are treated as linked" and is usually reviewed at payout; violations "can lead to an immediate hard breach, payout denial and a permanent blacklist", including "Removal of profits earned on the account". "All decisions by our Risk Team are final."
restrictiveRules.impact: Logging in from a device or shared VPS that another trader has used can lead, at payout review, to profits removed, the payout denied and the account closed.

restrictiveRules.program: All CFD plans — automated and coordinated trading
restrictiveRules.rule: Prohibited trading strategies (CFD): "high-frequency trading and arbitrage bots", reverse/latency/hedge arbitrage, "Trade emulators", strategies exploiting the absence of slippage, hedging between separate accounts and "Coordinated trading with other people, such as placing identical or opposing trades across different accounts" are prohibited. Copy trading "is only allowed between accounts you legally own." "Breaking these rules can lead to profits being removed, payouts being denied or your account being closed."
restrictiveRules.impact: Trades judged to be HFT, arbitrage, emulation or coordinated with another trader can cost the profits, the payout or the account.

restrictiveRules.rule: Terms (Trading Styles; Risk Management): "Blue Guardian may perform a risk review on accounts at any stage of the process" and may terminate or refuse a withdrawal if it deems the customer has not applied appropriate risk management. Prohibited Strategies (a)-(d) include undefined "excessive" risk per trade, cumulative risk and risk around news ("Boom or Bust"). Help article 'What happens if I break a rule?': Blue Guardian "can act on any account found to break our terms, even if the system didn't flag it at the time", may void profits and deny payouts; decisions are "final and binding".
restrictiveRules.impact: A payout can be refused after a later review on the basis of risk-taking the documents do not quantify.

restrictiveRules.rule: "Place at least one trade within your account's inactivity period": 30 days for all CFD accounts, counted from account creation (not from the first trade); otherwise "the account is treated as inactive and breached."

restrictiveRules.rule: "One payout only; crypto only, minimum $100." A request tops out at $250 profit ($225 at the 90% split). "After your payout, the account is permanently closed."

restrictiveRules.rule: "Your best day must be below 15% of your total profit", together with at least 5 trading days of 0.5% profit or more, before the single payout.

set.auditSummary: 18 November 2026 official post-16-Nov-2026 BrightFunded FAQ audit. set.auditSummary: Official-source review dated 19 November 2026. Clarity Traders LLC, a Delaware company, sells three simulated programmes from $5,000 to $200,000: Instant (no target, 3% daily limit that trails new equity highs, 5% maximum loss, from $95), One Step (10% target, 4% daily, 6% then 10% funded, from $59) and Two Step (8% and 5% targets, 5% daily, 8% then 10% funded, from $55). Per-size prices are only shown in a JavaScript checkout that could not be read. The terms state that payouts need KYC, 7 trading days and 14 days since the account was issued or the last request, and pass a consistency test (10% best-day share on Instant, 20% on funded One Step and Two Step). The split is 70% on the first payout, 80% on the second and 90% after, with 100% only through a paid add-on; payouts are in USDT every 14 days, or weekly with a paid add-on. The heaviest clauses are in Terms section 7: trades held under 60 seconds, hedging or coordinated trading across accounts and 'any strategy we reasonably determine is designed to exploit the program' are material breaches, for which a reward can be delayed, reduced or refused and the account closed without refund. A VPN ban, 60-day inactivity closure and an EA add-on also apply. On 19 November 2026 the Terms still contained unfilled placeholders (restricted-country list, account cap, daily reset time), and official pages disagree on whether weekend trading needs an add-on. Payout records and the company's legal file have not been independently verified.

restrictiveRules.rule: 'All trades must remain open for a minimum of 60 seconds.' The Terms (section 7) list 'Holding trades for less than 60 seconds' among practices that 'are a material breach'; section 8.7 allows the firm to 'delay, reduce or refuse a Reward' for a breach of section 7, and section 9.2 allows suspension or closure without refund for material breaches.
restrictiveRules.impact: Trades closed within 60 seconds can lead to a refused payout or account closure, not just exclusion of those trades.

restrictiveRules.rule: 'No single trading day can account for more than a 10% of your requested payout.' If the best day is above the share: 'Keep trading. Once your total profit is large enough that your best day falls under the limit, you can request.'
restrictiveRules.impact: A payout is delayed until total profit is at least ten times the best day.

restrictiveRules.program: One Step and Two Step — funded stage
restrictiveRules.rule: On funded accounts no single day can make up more than 20% of the requested payout (Terms 8.3 example: with a $1,000 best day, a request is possible once requested profit reaches $5,000).
restrictiveRules.impact: A payout is delayed until total profit is at least five times the best day.

restrictiveRules.rule: 'You receive 70% of eligible simulated gains on your first payout', 80% on the second and 90% from the third; 100% only with the paid 100% Profit Share add-on (+15% of the account price). Account cards advertise 'Up to 100%'.
restrictiveRules.impact: The first two payouts are paid at a lower split than the headline figure.

restrictiveRules.rule: 'Every funded account needs 7 trading days before a payout'; the Terms (section 8.1) also require that 'At least 14 days have passed since the Funded Account was issued'.
restrictiveRules.impact: The first payout cannot be requested before 7 trading days and 14 calendar days on the funded account.

restrictiveRules.rule: Terms section 2.2: 'You may not use a VPN or other means to hide your location.' Section 8.7 allows the firm to 'delay, reduce or refuse a Reward' for a breach of section 2; section 2.2 also says 'We may close Accounts opened from a restricted country.'
restrictiveRules.impact: Trading through a VPN can lead to a refused payout; this is stated only in the Terms.

restrictiveRules.rule: 'Automated trading is only allowed if you have purchased the EA's Allowed add-on' (+35% of the account price). High-frequency trading and latency arbitrage are not allowed; the Terms (section 7(4)) also prohibit 'Copy trading, signal services or trade-copying between accounts'.
restrictiveRules.impact: EA users must buy an add-on; copy trading is excluded.

restrictiveRules.rule: 'You must place at least one trade every 60 days.' Terms section 6.8: 'An Account with no trade for 60 days is closed as inactive.'
restrictiveRules.impact: An account idle for 60 days is closed.

restrictiveRules.rule: Terms section 7 lists practices that 'are a material breach', including 'Gap trading or other strategies designed to profit from the difference between simulated and real execution' (7.7) and 'Market manipulation, or any strategy we reasonably determine is designed to exploit the program' (7.8). Section 8.7 allows the firm to 'delay, reduce or refuse a Reward' for a breach and section 9.2 allows suspension or closure without refund for a material breach. The Terms say decisions are made 'in good faith, based on trade data' and that the trader is told which rule was breached and can respond.
restrictiveRules.impact: A strategy the firm determines is designed to exploit the program can lead to a refused payout or account closure; the clause does not define such strategies in advance.

restrictiveRules.rule: The trading-rules page says hedging is not allowed, including hedging or coordinating trades across accounts, also accounts held by other people. Terms section 7.3 lists 'Hedging, opposite-direction or coordinated trading across accounts' as a material breach (consequences in sections 8.7 and 9.2).
restrictiveRules.impact: Opposite-direction or coordinated trading across accounts can lead to a refused payout or account closure.

restrictiveRules.rule: The FAQ says 'weekend trading and holding positions over the weekend are permitted.' The trading-rules page says weekend trading is allowed only with the Trade on Weekends add-on. Terms section 6.6 says 'you may trade the news, hold positions overnight and over weekends', while section 6.7 says 'Trading on weekends is available only with the Trade on Weekends Add-on.'
restrictiveRules.impact: Official documents disagree on whether weekend trading needs a paid add-on; a trader should confirm in writing before trading at weekends.

restrictiveRules.rule: Terms section 2.2: 'The Services are not offered in countries subject to US, UN, EU or UK sanctions, or in [list of restricted countries / link]' and 'We may close Accounts opened from a restricted country.' The restricted-country list is an unfilled placeholder on 2026-11-19. Section 2.3: 'You must pass identity verification (KYC) before any Reward is paid'; section 8.7 allows a Reward to be delayed, reduced or refused over a KYC problem.
restrictiveRules.impact: Residents of a country the firm treats as restricted can have the account closed, and the published Terms do not list those countries.

set.auditSummary: Official-source review dated 19 November 2026. E8 Futures is the futures section of E8 Markets (shared branding and footer). It sells E8 Signature Futures (25K to 150K, list $120 to $450, 6% target, 2.66-4% end-of-day dynamic drawdown, 35% best-day rule, 80% split, no overnight positions) and E8 Zero (MAX 25K to 200K, list $228 to $1,088; Starter 25K to 150K), which has no daily loss limit, no consistency rule on the funded account and an 80% or 100% split. Prices for both programmes were shown at a discount with code E8. On the funded account, both programmes end after 4 payouts with per-cycle caps (for example $2,000-$3,000 on Signature $100K and $5,000 on Zero MAX $100K). Signature requires a buffer equal to the drawdown to stay in the account, and Zero states that profit left in the account 'can never be requested'. The E8 Funding LLC terms (Texas law, AAA arbitration) let E8 'withhold or revoke' payouts and decide 'in its sole discretion' whether to distribute one (5.1, 5.3), invalidate data generated through 'automation' (7.4, 9.1(a)), and terminate accounts for chargebacks or 'Prolonged account inactivity' without a defined period. They state payouts are processed within 7 days. Payout evidence and the regulatory status of the entities were not verified.

set.auditSummary: 18 November 2026 review of E8 official four-program comparison and programme-specific help pages. E8 One follows highest closed balance with dynamic 6% floor, locking at initial capital after enough gain, hard 4% daily limit and 40% funded best-day ratio. E8 Pro 8% static drawdown and 2.5% daily, but after first payout the floor jumps to initial capital: half each cycle profit is retained as a buffer, and 2% of initial account size is the maximum daily profit credited to targets/rewards. Zero Futures and Signature Futures use EOD dynamic drawdown that locks at starting capital, but Zero places 40% best-day consistency in evaluation and no funded concentration, whereas Signature places 35% in funded and a nonwithdrawable drawdown-sized buffer/payout caps. Official E8 size/pricing guide covers $5K–$500K for Classic and smaller Futures tiers, with variable checkout. There is no independent hands-on withdrawal or bank-level verification here; score 64 remains capped by existing Trustpilot notice.

restrictiveRules.impact: The advertised no-payout-cap programme still withholds half profit per cycle as account protection; high-profit days cannot accelerate the target beyond 2%.

The terms add that ETF may convert a trader to LIVE ELITE "at any time" at its sole discretion, and a trader who declines is prohibited from using ETF's services for two calendar years.

restrictiveRules.rule: Profit give-back rule: once the account reaches 20% profit, "Giving back more than 35% of accumulated profit can trigger the rule", checked at payout requests and risk audits. The terms state that an account with "a decline from its peak balance equal to 35% or more of the Account's gains" is "deemed invalid for continued participation in the Elite-Sim program".
restrictiveRules.impact: A drawdown of 35% of accumulated gains, even within the stated drawdown limit, can end the funded account.

restrictiveRules.rule: Traders must "place one valid trade per account each calendar week" and log in at least every 30 days. The terms state that failure to trade for a week without an approved break "will result in Account closure and void any otherwise eligible Rewards".

restrictiveRules.rule: Position limits: "1 mini equals 1 position. 10 micros equal 1 position." The page states that exceeding the limits can close the account and forfeit profits.
restrictiveRules.impact: Trading above the contract limit for the account size can end the account with its profits.

restrictiveRules.rule: Terms, Restrictions (ah): "All trades executed by you on ETF's platform shall have a minimum duration of ten (10) seconds"; such trades do not establish an Active Trading Day, and ETF may void a day already credited after notice. HFT is prohibited.
restrictiveRules.impact: Days built on trades shorter than 10 seconds do not count toward the active trading days required for each payout cycle.

restrictiveRules.rule: Terms, Restrictions (l): traders may not "utilize virtual private networks (VPNs), The Onion Router (TOR), virtual private servers (VPS), proxy servers"; ETF may audit "IP address logs and device fingerprints". restrictiveRules.impact: Trading through a VPN, VPS or proxy can lead to denied payouts and account termination.

restrictiveRules.rule: Terms, "Trading major economic events": "all Elite Accounts must be flat 5 minutes before the event to 5 minutes after the event starts."
restrictiveRules.impact: Positions must be closed around major economic releases on funded accounts.

restrictiveRules.rule: Terms, Restrictions (ac): use of "artificial intelligence (AI), bots, automated trading systems, trade copiers" is prohibited unless expressly authorised in writing by ETF; hedging across accounts with correlated instruments (e.g. NQ and MNQ) is also prohibited (o).
restrictiveRules.impact: Automated or copied trading needs written approval.

set.auditSummary: 18 November 2026 official product-date audit: StartTrader accounts purchased from 21 October 2026 use one 3%-target stage, 2% daily loss, 8% static overall loss, minimum three trading days, 60-day evaluation and an initial 5K tier. First daily limit breach is soft, second hard; a $400 lifetime payout maximum across two withdrawals applies to the model. SwiftTrader purchased from 15 July 2026 uses 6% target, 2% daily, 3% fixed total loss, 3%-of-starting-capital per profitable day evaluation cap, 60-day deadline and three trading days. ProTrader uses two targets of 8% then 6%, 5% daily and 10% fixed total risk; ProTrader Swing resets daily from the closed balance instead of EOD equity. Some older general help pages still show old StartTrader three-stage and former SwiftTrader loss percentages; the dated model pages govern newer purchases. Existing 77/100 retained pending contract reconciliation and no independent payout testing.

restrictiveRules.program: All Fintokei programmes — prohibited trading practices
restrictiveRules.rule: General Terms V17 art. V.2.xvii prohibit "gambling or unsustainable practices", listing among others overleveraging, one-sided bets, account rolling, "Achieving the Profit Target in one trade (or in a few similar trades on the same instrument within one day)" and "trading similar to randomness". Art. V.7: "the Company retains complete discretion to ascertain whether any activity, behaviour, or its characteristics fall" within these categories. Under art. V.3 the consequence can be failure of the Service conditions, suspension, and "you are not entitled to any performance reward payouts".
restrictiveRules.impact: Reaching a target or a large profit in one or a few trades can be classified by Fintokei as gambling, at its discretion, with loss of the related performance rewards. The criteria are only stated in the General Terms.

restrictiveRules.program: All Fintokei programmes — termination for non-compliance
restrictiveRules.rule: General Terms V17 art. XXII.7: non-compliance with listed articles of the Terms (or with regulatory/AML conditions), including on a suspicion of non-compliance, "represents a material breach"; Fintokei "is entitled to terminate any and all your Contract at any time without notice" and "you will lose the entitlement to any Performance reward etc. already paid or to be paid entirely."
restrictiveRules.impact: A breach, or a suspected breach, of the Terms can end every contract of the trader and remove entitlement to rewards both unpaid and already paid; the clause is only in the General Terms.

restrictiveRules.program: All Fintokei programmes — IP addresses, VPN and devices
restrictiveRules.rule: General Terms V17 art. V.2.vii, viii and x prohibit sharing one trading device between customers, giving account access to other persons, and using "multiple IP addresses from many countries"; "Trading IP's must show from the same region as the billing address." The help article on IP addresses says regular use of VPNs or proxies to hide or change the IP address is treated as a potential violation; if the practice continues without an exception, accounts may be terminated, with no refunds or payouts for breached accounts.
restrictiveRules.impact: Trading from an IP region different from the billing address, regular VPN/proxy use or a shared device can lead to termination of all accounts involved and loss of payouts. Occasional travel is allowed per the help article.

restrictiveRules.rule: General Terms V17 art. V.2.i prohibits latency arbitrage, reverse arbitrage, tick scalping and HFT. Appendix 1 (Ad 1): "placing trades that last less than 5 seconds is considered as "tick scalping" and is prohibited", with a 10% volume threshold; a warning is given first, then the account is breached.
restrictiveRules.impact: Repeated trades held under 5 seconds above the stated volume threshold lead to a warning, then an account breach.

restrictiveRules.program: All Fintokei programmes — EAs, signals and copy trading
restrictiveRules.rule: General Terms V17 art. V.2.ii-vi prohibit relying entirely on third-party signals, bots or software, EAs "on purpose created to" pass evaluations, copying other people's trades manually or via copy-trading systems, reverse copying between accounts, and using "the same or similar strategy" or trades as a mentor. Art. V.3: prohibited trading can mean "you are not entitled to any performance reward payouts".
restrictiveRules.impact: Copy trading, third-party signals or mirroring a mentor's trades can remove payout entitlement; the terms do not define "similar".

restrictiveRules.program: All Fintokei programmes — individually imposed restrictions
restrictiveRules.rule: The help article "Other restrictions that may be part of Consistency rules" (and General Terms art. V.3.ii-iii) says Fintokei may apply, "depending on your specific behavior", individual restrictions to active and future accounts: a 40% consistency rule (no single day may make 40% or more of the cycle profit, otherwise the payout is not processed until more profit is made), a net-positive policy (all active accounts must be at or above starting balance at the prior end of day before any payout), a daily profit cap of 1% (soft breach, account read-only until midnight UTC), reduced leverage, lot exposure and news limits, restricted instant payouts and reduced capital allocation. They can stay for an indefinite period and apply to future challenges; review possible after 3 to 6 months.
restrictiveRules.impact: If Fintokei applies these restrictions to a trader, payouts can be held until consistency or net-positive conditions are met across all accounts; the triggering criteria are not defined.

restrictiveRules.rule: General Terms V17 art. VII.B.4: "your account will be breached and closed if there is no trade made, open or closed in any 30-day period." Art. VI.7: a challenge not activated within 30 calendar days is suspended; renewal can be requested within 6 months, otherwise services end "without any right to a refund of the Price".
restrictiveRules.impact: An account with no trade for 30 days is breached; an unactivated challenge is lost without refund after 6 months.

restrictiveRules.program: All Fintokei programmes — KYC and information requests
restrictiveRules.rule: General Terms V17 art. VIII.2: Fintokei may request trade explanations, an interview, trading statements from other firms and source code of trading algorithms or API connections; "The Customer must respond to such inquiries within 24 hours of receiving the request." Art. VIII.5: failure to comply "will be considered a material breach of the Contract". Art. VIII.6: it is at the Company's "sole discretion to reject entering into the Virtually funded phase Contract for any or no reason". Art. II.2: restrictions apply by residence, nationality or registration; the banned-country list "may be adjusted from time to time".
restrictiveRules.impact: Missing the 24-hour reply window or a due-diligence request is a material breach (which art. XXII.7 links to loss of rewards); funded-phase entry can be refused without a reason.

restrictiveRules.rule: General Terms V17 art. V.5: "before processing any Performance reward payout, the Company may review your trading activity", with automated detection of prohibited trading (art. V.4); penalties are retracted only if the customer "can demonstrate otherwise beyond a reasonable doubt". The help article "When will I receive my payout?" says requests are "automatically approved within seconds" and contrasts this with manual reviews at other firms.
restrictiveRules.impact: The terms allow a review that can hold or refuse a payout, while the help centre describes automatic approval; the two official documents differ.

restrictiveRules.program: All Fintokei programmes — changes to conditions
restrictiveRules.rule: General Terms V17 art. IX.8: trading conditions and success parameters may change "without specific notification"; preamble 4: Fintokei may "update, change or replace any part of these Terms by posting updates", continued use meaning acceptance. Art. XXVI states changes are made "after giving you one month's notice or by posting updates and changes to our website". Art. XXVIII.8 keeps the previous StartTrader rules for StartTrader contracts bought before 21 October 2026.
restrictiveRules.impact: Success parameters of running accounts can change without individual notice; the notice period stated in the terms is inconsistent.

restrictiveRules.program: FTMO Account (non-Swing, after evaluation) and FTMO Instant Account — news
restrictiveRules.rule: FTMO "restricts order execution for 2 minutes before and 2 minutes after selected news releases" on symbols containing the affected currency or asset. The restriction "applies to any order execution, including your Stop Loss, Take Profit or any other pending orders." Swing accounts and accounts in the Challenge or Verification are exempt. "Violating this rule may result in termination of an FTMO Account / FTMO Instant Account."
restrictiveRules.impact: On a funded Standard or Instant account, a stop-loss or take-profit that fills inside the 4-minute window counts as a violation and can end the account; profits on it are not protected.

restrictiveRules.program: FTMO Account (non-Swing, after evaluation) and FTMO Instant Account — market breaks
restrictiveRules.rule: FTMO "restricts holding positions through market breaks longer than 2 hours"; all positions must be closed before such a break. Swing accounts and accounts in the FTMO Challenge or Verification are exempt. Violating it "may result in termination of an FTMO Account / FTMO Instant Account."
restrictiveRules.impact: Funded Standard and Instant traders must be flat before weekends and other breaks over two hours; a position left open can end the account.

restrictiveRules.rule: The Forbidden Trading Practices page bans "gap trading", defined as opening trades when major events are scheduled, or "two hours or less before a relevant financial market is closed for at least two hours." Possible consequences include "forfeiture of any potential Rewards" or "termination of all agreements you have with us." The page does not exempt Swing or evaluation accounts, while the FAQ says Swing and evaluation accounts may hold positions through news and market breaks.
restrictiveRules.impact: A Swing or evaluation trader relying on the FAQ exemption could still be found to have opened a position too close to a scheduled event or weekend close; which text prevails is not stated.

restrictiveRules.program: All FTMO accounts — forbidden trading practices
restrictiveRules.rule: Trades that "contradict how trading is actually performed in the financial markets (e.g., overleveraging, overexposure, one-sided bets, account rolling)" are forbidden, as is opening "substantially larger position sizes compared to your other simulated trades, on any of your accounts" or a "substantially smaller or larger number of positions". None of these terms is quantified. A breach "may result in corrective actions, including, but not limited to" removal of trades, "forfeiture of any potential Rewards" or termination of all agreements.
restrictiveRules.impact: Rewards can be forfeited for sizing or exposure judged excessive without a published threshold; the trader cannot check compliance in advance.

restrictiveRules.program: All FTMO accounts — capital allocation and identical strategies
restrictiveRules.rule: "The total capital allocation across all accounts and products is limited to $400,000 per trader or strategy" (before scaling; higher with the Premium Programme). Where trading is identical or substantially similar across accounts, including trades copied from the same third-party source, and the total exceeds the limit, FTMO "reserves the right to suspend the affected accounts." The strategy FAQ warns a third-party EA can lead to being "denied the FTMO Account" under this rule.
restrictiveRules.impact: A trader using a commercial EA or signal also used by unrelated FTMO clients can have accounts suspended or a funded account refused because of other people's capital, which the trader cannot see.

Section 18 (Termination): "If in our sole judgment you fail, or we suspect that you have failed" to comply, FTUK may end the agreement immediately and deny access; it "may terminate this agreement at any time without notice".

restrictiveRules.program: All FTUK programmes — IP region (Terms section 12 vs help centre)
restrictiveRules.rule: Terms section 12 lists as prohibited "Using multiple IP addresses from many countries or masking IPs" and states "Trading IP's must show from the same region as the billing address." The current help-centre article instead allows trading from another country after contacting support beforehand, and does not mention the billing address.
restrictiveRules.impact: A trader who travels and follows the help-centre procedure may still be outside the wording of the terms, which require the IP region to match the billing address; the two official texts do not say which prevails.

restrictiveRules.rule: The restricted-strategies list includes "Gambling and account churning", "Anti-Scaling", "Tick scalping" and several arbitrage types; the article does not define account churning, anti-scaling or tick scalping on the page. "Engaging in any of these banned strategies will result in account closure."
restrictiveRules.impact: Undefined categories such as gambling and account churning can close the account; what qualifies is left to FTUK's assessment.

restrictiveRules.rule: The account-breaches article lists a breach "if an account remains inactive for 30 days"; it does not define what counts as activity.
restrictiveRules.impact: An account left untraded for 30 days is breached.

restrictiveRules.program: All FTUK funded accounts — payout review
restrictiveRules.rule: "Each payout cycle is assessed independently and is subject to a full risk review at any point." Some payouts are approved automatically, and a previous approval does not confirm that past trading complied: "It is the sole responsibility of each trader to ensure that all trading activity" follows the rules. FTUK "reserves the right to request an interview with any trader at any time"; the account is view-only while a payout is pending.
restrictiveRules.impact: An earlier approved payout does not protect the same trading behaviour from being found in breach at a later review; trading is frozen while a request is pending.

restrictiveRules.rule: The Instant Funding programme table lists a -2% "account protector (max floating loss)". The account-breaches article states that on FLEX Funded and Instant Funding accounts "the account will be automatically terminated" after two Account Protector triggers.
restrictiveRules.impact: Two occurrences of open losses beyond 2% end an Instant Funding account even if the 5% daily and 6% maximum limits were not reached.

restrictiveRules.rule: The programme table sets a consistency score "Below 20%" at Levels 1-2, "Below 30%" at Levels 3-5 and "Below 40%" at Level 6.
restrictiveRules.impact: A payout is not eligible until no single day exceeds the stated share of profit for the current level.

restrictiveRules.rule: On the funded Flex account, the best winning day must be below 20% of the requested profit at Level 1, with the limit rising (up to 40%) as the account scales.
restrictiveRules.impact: A profitable payout request can be ineligible until the best-day ratio is met. (Split out of existing rule 0, see staleRules.)

restrictiveRules.rule: Overnight and weekend holding is "Allowed", but "you may partially close a position during the day, but the rest must be closed the same trading day"; a partially closed position cannot be held overnight.
restrictiveRules.impact: Scaling out of a position commits the trader to closing the remainder before the day ends.

set.auditSummary: 18 November 2026: FTUK's official help centre states every forex or futures position must stay open at least 30 seconds, even when a stop-loss or take-profit closes it sooner. Restricted strategies include martingale, grid, anti-scaling, tick and ultra-fast scalping, with account closure specified for prohibited practices. The current IP/VPN policy permits a single consistent address and ordinary mobile/home changes, but concurrent differing IP addresses, server switching, hidden-country location and unapproved overseas trading can lead to denied rewards and closure; traders must alert support before trading while abroad. The company reviews each withdrawal against logs, KYC and these conditions. A November Trustpilot account alleges a prior strategy approval followed by payout denial over seven sub-30-second trades; FTUK's public reply confirms applying the 30-second requirement, while the broader merits and communications are not independently established. The firm's claimed average payout speed and totals are not independently reconciled. Trustpilot now shows 3.9/5 from 811 reviews with no rating-withholding banner. Programme-specific drawdowns independently sourced 18 November: Flex Challenge 6% trailing on closed-balance highs, freezing at starting capital, plus 5% daily reset from the higher of equity or balance; forex Instant Funding 6% balance-relative trailing with the same eventual lock and 5% daily limit; FLEX Futures EOD trailing 2.67–4% with different evaluation versus funded daily-loss rules; Instant Sim Funding EOD trailing with $1,000–$5,250 limits and equity-triggered hard breaches. Older One-Step uses 8% relative trailing and the discontinued Two-Step 8% static, neither should be presented as a currently sold challenge. The verified firm-wide drawdown label is hybrid precisely because different available programmes use different mechanics. Score 72 to 65 for stringent enforceable rules and contested application, not for a proven company closure or fake-review campaign.

restrictiveRules.rule: Rule 1 payout criteria: trade notional size within MIN(median x 2.5, Q3 + 1.5 x IQR); at least 10 closed trades and 3 active trading days; QC score (2nd + 3rd best trade profit) / best trade profit >= 0.90. Failing it is 'NOT a violation': the payout is held until the metrics recover. A trader who passes Phase 2 without meeting it is placed in a Silver Funded account (2.0% risk), upgraded to a regular Pro account after 3 successful payouts.
restrictiveRules.impact: A profitable payout request can be held, and passing without meeting the criteria starts the funded stage on a lower-risk tier.

restrictiveRules.rule: Rule 2 position risk: a 'TOTAL' risk limit of 3.0% (Funded), 2.0% (Silver Funded) or 1.0% (Bronze Funded) across single positions, correlation buckets and the portfolio, computed from ATR when no stop loss is set at entry. 'Profits from violating trades are nullified, while losses remain'; serious or repeated violations move the account to a lower tier; removing or manipulating a stop loss to bypass the limit leads to 'immediate account termination regardless of the number of strikes'.
restrictiveRules.impact: Profits from trades over the risk limit are removed from the payout.

restrictiveRules.rule: Rule 3 execution: a violation occurs if trades closed in under 15 seconds exceed 2% of the total trade count, or trades under 30 seconds exceed 3%. Profits from violating trades are nullified and the account may be moved to a 'Restricted Professional Account' (Silver or Bronze tier).
restrictiveRules.impact: Profits from very short trades can be removed and the account downgraded.

restrictiveRules.rule: Rule 4 'Zero Tolerance Policy': copy trading, external signals, ready-made EAs producing identical entries, copying between Funded7 accounts, group trading, account sharing, hedge and latency arbitrage and martingale lead to 'Immediate Termination and Profit Forfeiture'; sharing detected 'via IP addresses, device IDs, or behavioral patterns' leads to immediate disqualification.
restrictiveRules.impact: Any of these practices ends the account and forfeits its profits.

restrictiveRules.rule: Rule 4 says a strategy may be terminated 'if the intent is identified as Tick Scalping' even when it does not trigger the Rule 3 duration limits, and a trader's own EA showing 'a high correlation with other traders' is treated as group trading. Terms Provision 1 lets the provider 'deny service to any individual at its sole discretion, at any time, and for any reason'.
restrictiveRules.impact: Termination with profit forfeiture can follow from the firm's assessment of intent or correlation, without a numeric threshold.

restrictiveRules.rule: Terms Provision 3: withdrawals are 'limited to USD 10,000 per calendar month, regardless of account size or trading performance'; amounts above can be moved to later months at the provider's discretion.
restrictiveRules.impact: Earned rewards above $10,000 in a month are deferred, whatever the account size.

restrictiveRules.rule: Terms Provision 15: an account that 'has no trading activity for 30 consecutive days' after trading began is terminated and cannot be reactivated (an account never traded within 30 days of issue can be reactivated on request).
restrictiveRules.impact: Thirty days without trading ends the account.

set.auditSummary: Deep desk audit (17 November 2026) of FundedElite's official FAQ. Regular 1-Step, 2-Step and Instant plans require a 21-day wait before the first reward request; subsequent windows are 14 days for regular 1/2-Step and 21 days for Instant, while Flash Activation/Catalyst operate on a different 14-day cycle. The advertised 95% share is an upper option, not the standard 80% payout for regular programs; Instant starts at 70% and later 80%. Consistency is product-specific: Instant 25%, Flash/Catalyst 30% unless removed by an add-on, certain large Lite accounts 60%, and the newer Elite Atom can impose 50% even on the funded stage. The official restricted-country FAQ explicitly excludes Turkey, Iran, Iraq and several other territories; use of a VPN to conceal a prohibited residence is a serious violation, although an innocent IP change may be reviewed as a soft breach. The earlier Trustpilot withheld-score/fake-review notice remains documented. No real-money payout, spread, slippage, legal residency eligibility or independent funding was tested.

restrictiveRules.program: FundedNext Stellar challenges and funded accounts — Quick Strike
restrictiveRules.rule: Profitable trades closed in under 30 seconds are measured as a share of all recorded profits. At 20% a warning; at ≥30% evaluation progression pauses. On funded accounts, ≥30% after warning can remove 100% Quick Strike profit and close the account at cycle-end.
restrictiveRules.impact: A trade stopped automatically under 30 seconds contributes if profitable; unlike an unconditional minimum duration, the 30% profit-concentration threshold and stage-specific consequences determine exposure.

restrictiveRules.program: FundedNext Stellar 1/2-Step and Lite — larger sizes
restrictiveRules.rule: Expert Advisors and the related VPS/EA add-ons are disallowed for new challenge sizes $50,000 and above; Lite/2-Step payout cycles and minimum phase-days vary by checkout choice and date.
restrictiveRules.impact: An automated strategy usable on a $25K account may not be allowed on a $50K account; a recently purchased Lite account follows two days, not a five-day legacy statement.

restrictiveRules.program: FundedNext Stellar Instant — news and rewards
restrictiveRules.rule: For trades in a correlated high-impact news ±5-minute window, only 40% of profitable P/L is credited to the account, while full losses count. Withdrawals need at least 1% growth or 5% growth for the EOD on-demand route.
restrictiveRules.impact: Headline profit can exceed eligible reward, with an EOD eligibility recheck if a new trade is placed.

restrictiveRules.program: Stellar 1-Step, 2-Step and Lite — FundedNext Account risk limit
restrictiveRules.rule: Traders must "limit risk to a maximum of 3% at any given time in the FundedNext Account", measured cumulatively across open positions and all entries of one trading idea, against the initial balance. First violation: warning and 100% of the violating trades' profit deducted from that cycle's reward. Second: 100% deduction and the account is permanently reclassified, "Allowable cumulative risk is reduced to 1% at a given time." If deductions reach the cycle's net profit, no reward is issued.
restrictiveRules.impact: Profitable trades that exceeded the risk ceiling are removed from the reward, and a repeat permanently lowers the allowed risk to 1%.

restrictiveRules.rule: "Gambling behaviors such as overleveraging, over-risking, a non-repeatable trading style" are enforced under the Risk parameter, identified from indicators such as losses outweighing average gains, breaching several accounts in a short span or unrealistic targets. The trader must then choose On-Demand Performance Rewards with a 40% Consistency Rule or an "Adjusted Profit Split" (percentage not stated); "it applies across all active FundedNext Accounts."
restrictiveRules.impact: A trader classified on these indicators gets either a consistency gate or a lower split on every active account; the reduced split is not published.

restrictiveRules.program: All Stellar programmes — discretionary Performance Reward
restrictiveRules.rule: The Performance Reward is granted "at its sole discretion" (Terms of Service, definitions); approval "does not, in itself, create an automatic entitlement" (12.2). Before payment FundedNext may "withhold, deny or reverse Performance Rewards" on "indications of fraud, abuse, manipulation or exploitation of failures" or KYC irregularities (12.6), and amounts may be "denied, withheld, cancelled, reversed, recovered, set off and/or clawed back" (9.8.1). The list of prohibited practices "is not exhaustive" (Challenge Terms 8.21).
restrictiveRules.impact: A reward is not owed until paid, and can be refused on 'indications' rather than a defined breach, including after it has been calculated.

restrictiveRules.rule: For prohibited conduct, including attempts or collusion, FundedNext may impose "a contractual penalty of up to $2,500 for each Prohibited Conduct" (Terms of Service 9.4(i)); the Challenge Terms (9.8) allow it per trade, strategy pattern, account, device or arrangement, and (9.9) allow it to be set off against amounts otherwise payable.
restrictiveRules.impact: Beyond losing a reward, a trader found in breach can owe money, deducted from pending rewards.

restrictiveRules.rule: Section 24 bans "acts of defamation, discrediting, disparagement, reputational attack or negative propaganda" on social media, forums, review platforms and in communications to third parties, including accusations "without verifiable factual basis". The user must remove content within 24 hours of notice; a breach is "a material breach" allowing FundedNext to "withhold, deny, adjust or reverse Performance Rewards" and impose a contractual penalty. Truthful reviews and regulator complaints are not expressly excluded.
restrictiveRules.impact: A negative public review can lead to rewards being withheld; 'disparagement' and 'negative propaganda' are not defined.

restrictiveRules.program: All Stellar programmes — devices, IP and VPN
restrictiveRules.rule: "Sharing devices with other traders is strictly prohibited, regardless of the relationship"; FundedNext states a "zero-tolerance stance" and "will terminate the account", with the reward or refund adjusted or denied. The Terms of Service ban "shared devices, shared IP environments, virtual machines, VPS clusters" shared with other users (9.1(u)) and VPNs or location spoofing (5.6), and allow device fingerprinting and IP checks (5.7).
restrictiveRules.impact: Two family members trading from the same computer or network can lose their accounts and rewards.

restrictiveRules.program: All Stellar programmes — cross-account hedging, copy trading and hyperactivity
restrictiveRules.rule: "Hedging across multiple accounts is prohibited" and "can result in account termination"; "Copy-Trading between multiple accounts not owned by the same individual" is prohibited. Hyperactivity is "200 trades or 2,000 server messages" in a day: warnings escalate and the third occurrence is a breach.
restrictiveRules.impact: Using a shared signal service or exceeding the daily trade count can end the account.

restrictiveRules.program: All Stellar programmes — market settlement window
restrictiveRules.rule: For trading during market settlement (00:00–02:00 server time), FundedNext "reserves the right" to review accounts, void trades or terminate the account. No threshold is stated.
restrictiveRules.impact: Trades opened around the daily rollover can be voided at the firm's discretion.

restrictiveRules.program: Stellar 1-Step, 2-Step and Lite — allocation and country caps
restrictiveRules.rule: Aggregate simulated capital is capped at $300,000 across Stellar 1-Step, 2-Step and Lite; passed challenges beyond the cap are paused before the FundedNext phase. Traders in Cambodia, Mongolia, Slovakia, Slovenia, Taiwan, Ukraine, the Czech Republic and Pakistan have a "maximum allocation of $50,000", and earlier buyers of $100,000 or $200,000 accounts there "will not be eligible to reset their account."
restrictiveRules.impact: Residents of the listed countries cannot be funded above $50,000 even if they bought and passed larger challenges.

restrictiveRules.rule: Challenge Terms 10.7: access is suspended if the customer "does not commence trading activity within thirty (30) calendar days of purchase".
restrictiveRules.impact: A challenge left unused for 30 days after purchase is suspended.

restrictiveRules.rule: One Phase 6% trailing and Standard 2-Phase 10% trailing; Classic 10%, Pro 8% and 3-Phase 5% fixed. Pro targets 4% then 8% and has minimum three 0.5%-positive days per phase/cycle.

restrictiveRules.rule: Classic has no evaluation consistency rule but 25% best-day concentration once funded; Pro has no such consistency requirement and uses ten-day payouts.
restrictiveRules.impact: A trader passing Classic quickly may need additional profit days to become payout-eligible.

restrictiveRules.program: Instant Funding Lite — news and protective exits
restrictiveRules.rule: Around high-impact news (±5 minutes), a trade closing via stop-loss or take-profit can remain subject to the news policy: profits of disallowed trades are removed while losses count. 20% best-day funded rule also applies.
restrictiveRules.impact: An automatic take-profit during the blackout may not be paid; this is a Lite-specific warning, not the rules of every 2-Phase product.

restrictiveRules.program: All programmes — prohibited strategies and discretion
restrictiveRules.rule: The General Terms ban trades contrary to real market practice "(E.G. OVERLEVERAGING, OVEREXPOSURE, ONE-SIDED BETS, ACCOUNT ROLLING, STATISTICAL ARBITRAGE)" (5.4.1.7) and "opening substantially larger position sizes compared to Customer's other trades"; "The Provider reserves the right to determine, at its own discretion, whether certain trades" are prohibited (5.4.3), and the prohibited list may be altered "AT ANY TIME" (5.4.1.8). High-frequency trading is described only as trades "in fractions of a second". The strategies FAQ states: "Engaging in prohibited strategies will result in account termination and voided profits."
restrictiveRules.impact: Profits can be voided for sizing or strategies FXIFY judges prohibited, without published thresholds.

restrictiveRules.rule: Herd trading and collusion are prohibited: "This includes using the same EA from the same company as it would lead to coordinated trades." Reverse and group hedging ("offsetting positions across accounts") is also prohibited. Consequence: "account termination and voided profits."
restrictiveRules.impact: A trader running a commercial EA that other FXIFY clients also run can have profits voided, regardless of independent intent.

restrictiveRules.rule: "Prohibited strategies are the same as FXIFY challenges" with one addition: "no EA's, bots or copytraders are allow" [sic].
restrictiveRules.impact: Any automated or copied trading on Instant Funding Lite falls under prohibited strategies (termination and voided profits per the strategies FAQ).

restrictiveRules.rule: The strategies FAQ lists "High Leverage News Trading: Placing large, leveraged positions around major news events, akin to gambling" as prohibited (termination and voided profits). FXIFY's prohibited-strategies article says high leverage news trading is allowed "within limits". Neither page defines the size or leverage that crosses the line.
restrictiveRules.impact: A trader cannot tell from official pages how large a news-time position may be before its profits are voided.

restrictiveRules.rule: "If you do not place a trade at least once every 60 days on your account ... we will consider you inactive and your account will be breached." The Instant Funding Lite FAQ states the same 60-calendar-day rule.
restrictiveRules.impact: An account with no trade for 60 days is breached.

restrictiveRules.program: Funded accounts — withdrawal frequency in the trader agreement
restrictiveRules.rule: The User Agreement (section 5, page modified 25 March 2025) says withdrawals "can be requested no more than once every 30 days", while FXIFY's current programme material describes shorter cycles (for example ten-day payouts on 2-Phase Pro). The agreement does not say which programmes the 30-day limit covers.
restrictiveRules.impact: The signed agreement allows a longer payout interval than the one advertised; which applies is not stated.

set.auditSummary: 18 November 2026 programme deep dive adds model-specific conditions to the existing 58/100 Trustpilot and payout-integrity review. 1-Step post-1-August 2026: 10% evaluation target, 3% daily, 6% static maximum, three profitable days; initial two payouts capped at 6% of initial size or $10K and profits above $3,000 on a day removed. 2-Step Standard: 8%/6% goals, 4% daily and 10% fixed total; funded GOAT Guard can cut the split to 50% at 2% simultaneous floating loss, and repeat breach closes, while some cheaper 1% Guard offers trigger immediate closure. Instant GOAT: 6% real-time equity trailing max, 3% daily, 2% simultaneous floating hard loss, 15% best-day and five days ≥0.5% before rewards. Instant Premium: 6% trailing, 1% floating hard loss for purchases after 2 September, five 0.5%-profitable days, no blanket concentration. Instant Daily: 3% real-time trailing, only 1% floating loss, expires after 30 days, payout per request limited to 1%-3% account size; payout locks floor at original capital, so emptying remaining profits can immediately breach. Existing initial reward restrictions, account matching, KYC and Trustpilot withhold notice remain intact. 58 points unchanged; do not assert review-removal attribution or universal programme rules.

restrictiveRules.rule: The first payout is generally eligible after 14 days from the first trade; certain products offer seven days or an Instant24 variant. All positions must be closed before requesting.
