restrictiveRules.program: All RZR Funded accounts — short-hold 'scalping' profits
restrictiveRules.rule: Terms clause 7: "Scalping shall be deemed to occur where the aggregate net profits derived from trades held for less than 3 minutes" make up "thirty percent (30%) or more of the total net profits" in the assessment period (not defined). "Isolated instances" below that threshold are not scalping. The Company may "adjust, reduce, or remove profits attributable to such trades", restrict, suspend or terminate the account; its determination is "final and binding".
restrictiveRules.impact: If trades under three minutes produce 30% or more of net profit, those profits can be removed and the account ended.

restrictiveRules.program: All RZR Funded accounts — prohibited trading enforcement
restrictiveRules.rule: Clause 7 lists Prohibited Trading, including "all or nothing trading": "Trading behavior that involves risking the entire daily loss limit or maximum drawdown" or a "substantial portion" of either on one or concurrent trades. Enforcement may include "withholding, cancellation, reduction, or recovery of simulated profits, revenue share, or payouts" and "Forfeiture of fees in cases of material breach"; "The Company may take proportionate enforcement action without prior notice, explanation, or evidence."
restrictiveRules.impact: Payouts can be withheld or clawed back on an undefined 'substantial portion' test, and the terms allow action without giving the trader evidence.

restrictiveRules.program: All RZR Funded accounts — linked IP, device or VPN
restrictiveRules.rule: Clause 7 prohibits operating or controlling multiple accounts, including "through the use of shared, masked, or linked device identifiers (including CID/Device ID), IP addresses, VPNs, proxies" or "virtual machines". Enforcement can extend to "existing, future, or technically connected accounts via IP address, device ID, CID, VPN, proxy".
restrictiveRules.impact: Accounts that share an IP, device or VPN exit with another account can be treated as one owner and sanctioned together, including withholding payouts.

restrictiveRules.program: All RZR Funded accounts — KYC and payout destination
restrictiveRules.rule: Clause 6: KYC may be requested at any stage and is required before any payout; "Payouts will only be made to a bank account or wallet held in the Customer's own name." If the customer fails or refuses KYC, or information is false or inconsistent, "the Company may reject any payout, forfeit simulated profits and close the Customer's accounts." Clause 3.2: services are "not available to residents of certain jurisdictions, including but not limited to the United Kingdom"; the rewards page says Instant programmes are not available to residents of the UK, Mauritius, Hong Kong and Singapore.
restrictiveRules.impact: Profits are forfeited if KYC fails or details are judged inconsistent, and payouts cannot go to a third-party account.

restrictiveRules.program: All RZR Funded accounts — Risk Management Group (retroactive)
restrictiveRules.rule: Clause 8: the Company may place a customer in a Risk Management Group (RMG) for activity that "appears to constitute Prohibited Trading". RMG imposes leverage caps on all existing and future accounts (FX 1:30, indices 1:5, commodities 1:5, metals 1:3, crypto 1:1) and possibly "reduced trade size, limited asset access, or temporary freezes", and lets the Company reclassify trades and adjust results. "RMG placement may apply retroactively to trading activity that occurred before placement is enforced." Removal follows "Successfully receiving three (3) payouts on a single RZR Funded account" or the Company's own decision.
restrictiveRules.impact: A trader flagged on an 'appears to' basis can see past trades reclassified and every account restricted until three further payouts are made.

restrictiveRules.program: All RZR Funded accounts — risk controls changed without notice
restrictiveRules.rule: Clause 3.6: "The Company may, at any time and without prior notice, apply, change or remove risk controls" on any account, including leverage, margin, position size, same-direction exposure, drawdown parameters and allocated capital, independent of any rule breach.
restrictiveRules.impact: Position-size and drawdown limits on a running account can change at any time without notice.

restrictiveRules.program: Challenge and funded accounts — same strategy across accounts above $400,000
restrictiveRules.rule: Clause 7 prohibits using the same or substantially similar strategy across multiple accounts "where the aggregate allocated or notional capital of such accounts exceeds USD 400,000", counting accounts "directly or indirectly controlled by the Customer" or coordinated with others. Hedging is allowed within one account but "prohibited across separate accounts". General clause 7 enforcement applies.
restrictiveRules.impact: Copying one's own strategy over several accounts totalling more than $400,000 can lead to payouts being withheld and accounts closed.

set.payoutDelay: Most models: eligible after 14 days from first trade (7 with add-on); Instant24 after its 24h window. Company guarantees risk-team approval or rejection within 24 business hours only for otherwise eligible requests; bank/crypto delivery is not covered.
set.verdict: RZR Funded, the October 2026 successor brand to Hantec Trader, has a live site, named legal entities and detailed model-by-model trading rules. Its base profit share is 80% (up to 95% with an add-on), and the advertised 24-hour reward promise concerns approval, not actual receipt. Recent mixed payout reviews and hard-breach conditions justify monitoring, while the firm's live rules and Trustpilot 4.4/5 are more substantive than a closure rumour. PropRadar score: 70/100.
set.auditSummary: 18 November 2026: RZR Funded is commercially active at rzrfunded.com after the 19 October Hantec Trader rebrand. Its own guide states 80% standard reward share, 95% only with an add-on, 14-day typical request cycle measured from the first trade, and model-specific 7-day or Instant24 exceptions. Instant Lite requires five profitable days of at least 0.5%, Enhanced three; open trades must be closed before submitting. The 24-business-hour guarantee covers approval or rejection by the risk team, not arrival of funds, and expressly excludes requests under investigation, verification, possible rule breaches or incorrect details. Separate official rules list hard closure for drawdown/open-risk/inactivity breaches; the site distinguishes some soft rule violations. Trustpilot currently shows 4.4/5 from 880 reviews on the claimed, merged profile. Individual payout refusal allegations remain disputed and were not independently adjudicated. RZR's contract identifies the Saint Lucia operator and simulation-only service; marketing association with Hantec's regulated broker group must not be mistaken for broker protection. Score revised 73 to 70 to reflect the operational conditions and short post-rebrand track record.

restrictiveRules.program: 2-Step Pro / Prime and 1-Step Prime — funded withdrawal choice
restrictiveRules.rule: Pro/Prime bi-weekly rewards require three profitable days at at least 0.5% initial balance; monthly rewards require seven. On-demand rewards require at least 2% total gain and a 40% best-day consistency ceiling.
restrictiveRules.impact: The headline profit share and payout speed depend on the chosen cycle; an eligible trading profit is not automatically available for immediate withdrawal.

restrictiveRules.program: 1-Step Fly / 2-Step Fly — evaluation versus funded stage
restrictiveRules.rule: Fly evaluations have static maximum losses, but simulated funded stages use intraday trailing limits; challenge news-window trades and weekend holds can result in termination. Evaluation consistency is 40% for 1-Step Fly or 50% in phase 2 for 2-Step Fly.
restrictiveRules.impact: A trader may pass under a static loss floor and then face a materially different trailing floor and stage-specific restrictions; funded payout split differs from challenge marketing.

restrictiveRules.program: Direct and Direct Fly — funded accounts
restrictiveRules.rule: Direct is subject to an end-of-day trailing floor, 20% consistency on bi-weekly payouts and restricted news/weekend operation; Direct Fly has an intraday trailing floor. The published matrix describes rule breaches with possible account termination.
restrictiveRules.impact: The two direct routes must not be described as equivalent instant-funding accounts, and paid fees are exposed to a breach during restricted trading windows.

restrictiveRules.program: All Hola Prime accounts — gambling, speculative and inconsistent trading
restrictiveRules.rule: Section 22 of the terms prohibits "abusive or exploitative trading strategies such as, but not limited to, gambling", including practices that "resemble gambling rather than a structured and repeatable trading strategy" or are "materially dependent on concentrated, excessive, or non-repeatable trading outcomes". Section 22.3.5 also prohibits significant deviations from a trader's proven strategy (switching between EA and manual trading, changing asset classes, margin use or risk exposure), which "may result in an account review, suspension or denial of Performance Rewards". Where Risk Management finds prohibited trading, or conduct that "in our reasonable assessment" is designed to circumvent the policies, it "will result in forfeiture of any accrued trader payout, and fees paid to the Company".
restrictiveRules.impact: Accrued payouts and fees can be forfeited on the firm's own assessment of what counts as gambling-like or inconsistent trading; the terms give no objective threshold.

restrictiveRules.program: All Hola Prime accounts — VPN, restricted countries and shared devices
restrictiveRules.rule: The prohibited-practices page bans "Using a VPN to circumvent geographical restrictions or disguise access from a restricted country or region" and "Trading from another trader's device, sharing laptops, desktops, tablets, or mobile phones with other traders"; restricted-country access or VPN routing through a restricted country "will lead to account termination". Terms section 20 adds that "the use of VPNs or VPS to bypass restrictions or the rules are strictly prohibited".
restrictiveRules.impact: A login routed through a restricted region or a device shared with another participant can end the account, whatever its profit.

restrictiveRules.program: All Hola Prime accounts — EAs, copy trading and HFT
restrictiveRules.rule: EAs "are permitted only on MT5 accounts where the EA usage add on has been purchased"; prohibited EA activity "may result in account cancellation and permanent ban" with fees non-refundable. Copy trading is allowed only between accounts owned by the same person, limited to "a maximum of one Master Account and one Copier Account" on funded accounts, and copying from other prop firms is "strictly prohibited" (accounts purchased on or after 15 September 2026); breaches mean "all associated accounts will be immediately terminated". Tick scalping/HFT with "sophisticated expert advisers" is not allowed.
restrictiveRules.impact: Automated or copied trading outside these limits can end every linked account; EA use requires a paid add-on.

restrictiveRules.rule: Terms section 21.9 sets a Maximum Position Size, "the highest total number of lots you are permitted to hold open at any moment". For 2-Step Pro Forex a breach closes all open trades and disables the account; "Profits from trades that exceeded the specified limits will be deducted from the account", and a second breach brings "a reduction of the remaining profit split to 30%" and termination.
restrictiveRules.impact: Profit from oversized positions is removed, and a repeat breach cuts the split to 30% and ends the account. The section names 2-Step Pro only; the audited key groups Pro and Prime.

restrictiveRules.program: 1-Step Prime, 2-Step Prime / Pro and Direct (Forex) — risk per trade idea
restrictiveRules.rule: Terms section 21.11: "The Risk Limit means that the total potential loss across all positions based on the same trading idea must not exceed X%", 2% on these Forex accounts. Stop-loss orders are mandatory; a trade closed without one is treated as carrying infinite risk.
restrictiveRules.impact: Positions sized above 2% of risk per idea, or without a stop loss, breach the rule regardless of outcome.

restrictiveRules.program: 1-Step / 2-Step Fly and Direct Fly — funded order size
restrictiveRules.rule: A note in terms section 21.9 caps orders at 5 lots per order on 1-Step Fly, 2-Step Fly and Direct Fly simulated funded accounts. The consequence of exceeding it is not stated separately.
restrictiveRules.impact: Funded Fly and Direct Fly traders cannot scale a single order above 5 lots.

restrictiveRules.program: All Hola Prime accounts — KYC interview before first payout
restrictiveRules.rule: Terms section 8.2.3: "Customers are required to complete a mandatory KYC verification interview before their first payout is processed", and a follow-up interview may be requested "at any stage". Section 8.6: "Failure to pass the KYC verification process will result in the rejection of the Customer's account application" with no refund of fees; failing AML screening counts as failing KYC.
restrictiveRules.impact: The first payout depends on passing an interview; a failed KYC or AML check ends the account without a fee refund.

restrictiveRules.program: Forex simulated funded and Direct accounts — country allocation cap
restrictiveRules.rule: Terms section 21.12: "Maximum capital allocation will be restricted to $90K for below countries": Nigeria, Malaysia, Indonesia, Cambodia, Israel, Thailand, Botswana, Mongolia, Kazakhstan, Jamaica, Mozambique (the general Forex cap is $400K).
restrictiveRules.impact: Residents of these 11 countries can hold far less funded capital than the advertised maximum.

restrictiveRules.rule: Terms section 21.5: "Accounts inactive for 30 consecutive calendar days will be permanently suspended." Only an opened trade counts; modifying SL/TP or placing pending orders does not.

set.verdict: Hola Prime publishes detailed, product-specific simulated trading rules, identifies multiple platform/legal entities and has 4.6/5 on Trustpilot from 4,324 reviews. A payout-processing review commissioned from Deloitte and examined by financial press offers more documentation than normal industry self-reporting, but the company itself expressly says the engagement was neither a full audit nor an assurance opinion; the report is not published and the fast-processing figures cover a defined set of eligible requests. Some users dispute account restrictions and payment decisions. PropRadar raises the score cautiously from 64 to 67/100 for transparency, not a guarantee of solvency or future rewards.
set.auditSummary: 17 November 2026: Hola Prime's published rulebook distinguishes static maximum loss limits on some Prime/Pro evaluations, intraday trailing rules on Fly funded programmes and end-of-day trailing limits on Direct. Payout timing and reward shares depend on each selected schedule; its own Fly schedules have differed on whether the split is 70% or 80%, so a universal split should not be inferred. The footer identifies separate Hong Kong, Cyprus, Mauritius and technology-provider roles; Mauritius investment-dealer authorisation for one related broker entity is not equivalent to investor protection for every simulated challenge. Finance Magnates reported reviewing materials from the Deloitte-commissioned payout-processing exercise for 15 October 2025–15 March 2026. The seller's summary says 98.35% of requests with complete information were processed within one hour, 1.65% later and no denials in the scoped reviewed population. Crucially, the same summary says this is NOT an audit or assurance opinion, the full report is not publicly distributed and the engagement was not designed for third-party reliance. These percentages therefore do not establish that all people buying challenges qualified, that bank deposits were independently reconciled or that future payments are guaranteed. Trustpilot currently displays 4.6/5 on 4,324 reviews with both positive experiences and contested payout/KYC restrictions. Balanced score: 67/100, below the independently established, multi-year industry leaders.

restrictiveRules.rule: New November 2026 crypto Instant model: 3% daily loss and 5% fixed lifetime loss. A completed position losing over 2% of initial balance causes one non-resetting warning and the second such violation fails the account; margin is capped at 25% of initial balance and combined open notional at 2 times initial balance.
restrictiveRules.impact: Instant funding removes the evaluation but has separate trade-level and exposure constraints besides the standard drawdown floors.

restrictiveRules.rule: Before the first reward, three qualifying UTC trading days and a positive account result are required. A qualifying day needs a closed trade worth at least 5% of initial capital with a move of at least 1% of that trade value before fees.
restrictiveRules.impact: An ordinary day with a small closed position does not necessarily count toward the first three required days.

restrictiveRules.rule: Each request includes no more than the first 5% of initial capital in account profit, split 80% by default; after a request the funded account resets. The fee is normally non-refundable, and the company describes these as simulated accounts.
restrictiveRules.impact: A $100K Instant account ordinarily caps a single gross reward pool at $5K and trader share at $4K before any discretionary profit-split increase.

restrictiveRules.program: Hyro Core, One-Step and Two-Step — evaluation consistency
restrictiveRules.rule: The official trading-rules page limits the contribution of any single evaluation trading day to 40% of the required profit target. This applies to challenges, not automatically to Instant funded payouts.
restrictiveRules.impact: One profitable day can be too concentrated to complete an evaluation even when the total profit target is achieved.

restrictiveRules.program: Funded accounts — profit above 5% per request
restrictiveRules.rule: "The profit counted in one payout request is capped at 5% of your initial balance", and "If a trader does not withdraw and exceeds 5% profit, any additional profit will not be paid." The FAQ does not limit this to one programme. Terms 11.7 add that payouts are subject to "the per-payout and cumulative limits published in the payout information on the Platform".
restrictiveRules.impact: A funded trader who lets profit run beyond 5% of the initial balance before requesting a payout loses the excess; a cumulative limit is also referenced but its value was not found.

restrictiveRules.program: Core, One-Step and Two-Step — funded exposure limits
restrictiveRules.rule: On funded accounts "A trader may allocate up to 25% of the initial account balance as total margin across open positions" and total open notional may not exceed twice the initial balance. Each limit allows one formal warning; the next breach fails the funded stage. These limits do not apply during the evaluation.
restrictiveRules.impact: Position sizing that was acceptable in the evaluation can fail the funded account after one warning.

restrictiveRules.rule: Prohibited practices include "any strategy that in the Provider's reasonable and good-faith view does not reflect genuine trading skill and instead exploits the mechanics of the Challenge" (10.2(g)), "materially changing your strategy, instrument set or risk profile between the Challenge or Verification and the Funded Trader Phase in a manner that defeats the purpose of the evaluation" (10.2(n)) and advantages "not replicable in live market conditions" (10.2(k)). Consequences may include voiding trades, failing the challenge and forfeiting "any pending rewards" (10.3). Before (b)-(f) apply, the trader is notified and has at least 14 calendar days to make representations; the detection method is not disclosed.
restrictiveRules.impact: Pending rewards can be forfeited on a judgement about 'genuine trading skill' or a change of strategy after passing; the terms do provide notice and a 14-day right to respond.

restrictiveRules.program: All programmes — hedging across accounts and connected persons (Terms 10.2A)
restrictiveRules.rule: Opposing or offsetting positions across two or more of the trader's accounts, or with accounts of a "connected person" (household or family member, anyone sharing a device, network, payment card or wallet), including correlated-instrument and basket hedges, are prohibited. The firm may conclude this from timing, sizing or net exposure, without showing intent, and may void trades, fail challenges, retain deposits and "forfeit any reward accrued but not yet paid on any Trading Account involved". Hedging inside a single account is permitted.
restrictiveRules.impact: Unrelated trading by a household member on the same network can be treated as cross-account hedging unless the shared use was disclosed under 4.5A; unpaid rewards on every linked account are at risk.

restrictiveRules.rule: Where the firm "reasonably suspects" "suspicious behaviour, gambling-style trading, or exploitation", it may reduce the account size or tier, cap exposure, position size or risk per trade idea, reduce leverage or remove instruments. The measure applies prospectively only, is not a finding of breach and does not by itself forfeit a reward; the detection method is not disclosed. In the funded phase the Funded Trader Entity exercises the equivalent right (FTA clause 7.11).
restrictiveRules.impact: Account size and therefore future rewards can be reduced on suspicion of undefined 'gambling-style trading', without a breach finding.

restrictiveRules.rule: KYC (via Sumsub) is "a mandatory condition of any payout". If KYC is not completed when requested, "any rewards, profits, or balances accrued may be deemed void" after notice and a 30-day window (11.5). If the trader becomes "resident in, a citizen of, or physically located in" a Prohibited Jurisdiction (list of 22 countries plus five Ukrainian regions), the firm "may terminate your Account and forfeit pending rewards" (12.4). The list can change immediately on publication when sanctions require (12.5).
restrictiveRules.impact: Travelling to, or a sanctions-driven listing of, a prohibited country can cost pending rewards; failing a KYC request can void accrued profit.

restrictiveRules.rule: "If your Account is inactive for a period of ninety (90) consecutive calendar days (no login and no simulated trade), the Provider may close your Account on fourteen (14) days' prior notice by email."
restrictiveRules.impact: An account with no login and no trade for 90 days can be closed after a 14-day email notice.

restrictiveRules.rule: VPNs are permitted for privacy, but not to conceal the jurisdiction of operation. If VPN use is detected the firm may request proof of residence; "failure to provide such proof within fourteen (14) calendar days may result in Account suspension pending review." VPN use to reach Tealstreet or Tiger terminals from a restricted jurisdiction is prohibited (12.6A).
restrictiveRules.impact: A VPN user may have to prove residence within 14 days or have the account suspended pending review.

set.auditSummary: 18 November 2026 review of HyroTrader's newly launched Hyro Instant crypto account, distinct from its One-Step, Two-Step and Hyro Core challenges. The issuer advertises sizes $5K–$100K with normally nonrefundable prices $169–$2,799, 3% daily and 5% static overall limits, a 2% maximum losing-position strike rule and separate margin/notional caps. set.auditSummary: Deep audit (17 November 2026): IC Funded's current 2-Step Professional rules specify a 10% Step 1 and 5% Step 2 target, 5% daily limit calculated on end-of-day equity, 10% fixed overall drawdown, and three active days per evaluation step. The page advertises $74 for a $5K evaluation, up to 90% profit share, biweekly payout availability (weekly only as an add-on), and graduated profitable-day checks: five for the first reward, three for the second, none thereafter, subject to 14-day intervals. Current Terms section 12 prohibits latency/price exploitation, artificial target-meeting trades and certain automation; it gives the operator broad rights to cancel rewards on violations. The terms explicitly distinguish simulated capital from live market funds; KYC and jurisdictional eligibility still apply. Unlike 2-Step, the Instant program advertises at most 80% reward share, so a single firm-level figure must not be read as every product's default. Spread, platform execution and bank/on-chain payment evidence were not independently tested; no Trustpilot manipulation allegation is inferred.

set.verdict: Instant Funding's product name conceals materially distinct risk models: Instant Funding Pro uses a 10%-to-5% smart drawdown lock, while One-Phase Pro and Two-Phase use genuinely static maximum limits. Per-idea risk caps, best-day payout rules and a required drawdown lock can block payouts or terminate accounts despite profitable performance. PropRadar retains 64/100 under its pre-existing Trustpilot-withheld-rating cap; no independently bank-verified blanket payout conclusion is claimed.
set.auditSummary: 18 November 2026: compared current official Instant Funding Pro, One-Phase Pro, Two-Phase and maximum-loss help pages. Pro (formerly Smart) begins at a 10% static-floor distance, but once closed account balance gains 5%, the floor tightens to 5% below the original starting capital and is locked, a hybrid model rather than ordinary static or continuously trailing. A payout request needs this lock; first eligible request follows 14 days, later every seven. One-Phase Pro instead uses 8% static maximum, 3% daily reset from higher balance/equity, 10% evaluation target, 3 separate evaluation days, funded 40% best-day limit and risk-per-idea at 50% of starting daily drawdown with ten-minute aggregation. Two-Phase uses 10% static max and 5% daily, 8% then 5% targets, matching funded best-day/risk-per-idea restrictions and asset-class lot limits. Some other micro, crypto, lite and starter variants have distinct thresholds in the same official table and are not automatically assigned a main-programme rule. Prior documented Trustpilot rating-withheld and profile-merger notice is retained without attributing review-origin wrongdoing to the firm. No live-trade test or independently authenticated individual payout was obtained. Score remains capped at 64/100.

Opposite trades across accounts or prop firms (group hedging) are prohibited.

restrictiveRules.program: All Lark accounts — VPN/VPS during identity checks

restrictiveRules.impact: Completing identity verification through a VPN can stop funding or breach a funded account.

restrictiveRules.rule: "We require traders to place at least one trade every 30 days to keep their accounts active." An account breached for 30 days of inactivity can ask support to lift the breach; reinstatement is not guaranteed after a long period.

restrictiveRules.program: Single-share CFDs — earnings, dividends and corporate actions
restrictiveRules.rule: Holding a single-share equity CFD position through an earnings release, dividend distribution or other corporate action is prohibited; positions must be closed by 3:50 pm ET on the event day (or the previous trading day for pre-market events). A violation is "an immediate, hard breach of your account" and gains or losses on the position are removed from all gain calculations.
restrictiveRules.impact: One share CFD held through earnings ends the account, separately from the general 'no news restrictions' statement.

restrictiveRules.program: Instant Master Account — trailing drawdown on the funded account
restrictiveRules.rule: "8% Max Trailing Drawdown Limit": "The breach level trails the highest closed balance recorded on the account" and locks at the initial balance once the account reaches an 8% gain or when the first payout is requested; it "does not reset upon requesting a payout."
restrictiveRules.impact: Profit on the Instant account raises the breach floor until the 8% lock, so withdrawals are made against a moving limit.

restrictiveRules.program: All Lark accounts — payout processor availability
restrictiveRules.rule: Restricted: Iran, North Korea, Myanmar, the Russian Federation, Belarus and Quebec. "We currently process payouts through Riseworks, so please ensure that it is available in your country and region." The article states no consequence if Riseworks is unavailable.

set.auditSummary: Official-source deep review dated 17 November 2026. Lark Funding allows VPNs and VPSs for trading while discouraging them because network anomalies can trigger additional scrutiny; it explicitly prohibits VPN usage during KYC/AML identity checks, where it may lead to refusal or a breach. Standard 1-Step, 2-Step and 3-Step payout requests follow 14-day cycles, unlike the Instant product whose first request is on demand but subsequent withdrawals are 30 days apart. There is a $100 minimum withdrawal and a stated $40 charge for each payout; processing is advertised within three business days, not guaranteed bank receipt. The firm excludes Myanmar, Iran, North Korea, Russia, Belarus and other jurisdictions, but absence from an exclusion list alone does not confirm local regulatory permission in India, China or Singapore. Its homepage has previously shown contradictory product-card reward/drawdown labels, so account-specific checkout terms take precedence. Trustpilot's older 4.3/5 snapshot is a public review aggregate, not proof of independently settled rewards, and PropRadar did not test spreads, slippage, account opening or receipts.

A funded account not eligible for live is refunded its evaluation cost only if at least 50% of its drawdown remains. Household members may not trade sim once one member trades live.

restrictiveRules.rule: Minimum request $500. Maximum per request: Payouts 1-3 $1,000 / $2,000 / $2,500 / $3,000 and Payouts 4-5 $1,000 / $2,500 / $3,000 / $3,500 for 25K / 50K / 100K / 150K. A trade before processing that drops profit below the goal may cause the request to be denied.

restrictiveRules.rule: Section 4(b) of the LucidDirect agreement (last modified 19 May 2025): 'Your Balance shall at no time exceed $35,000 (the "Maximum Balance")', and profits above it are 'disregarded and inapplicable to any future calculation of a Reward Balance'. The current help-centre payout page does not mention this cap.

set.auditSummary: Deep audit (17 November 2026): Moneta Funded Ltd is disclosed in Saint Lucia (2025-00532); its September 2026 contract defines simulated funds and account-specific rules, not deposits at Moneta Markets. Its program comparison spans 1-Step Daily, 1-Step, 2-Step, Instant, Instant Pro, Phoenix and Sprint. The comparison marks news trading disallowed on the ordinary 1/2-Step and Instant models but allowed on Instant Pro and Phoenix, with material differences in loss limits and first payout. For Instant, it states a 15%/20% consistency threshold; clause 5.1F of the current PDF calculates best realized trading day divided by total realized P&L in that payout cycle, delaying payment when breached. The PDF also allows automatic closing or excluding profit above an Instant Pro per-day cap. At the time of review, the public general-rules page described 1-Step/Phoenix as 6% static while the comparison presented its generic One-Step as 5% trailing: this may reflect product variants or stale copy, so obtain the exact program/checkout document in writing. Advertised 14-day/on-demand reward cycles are not authenticated customer payout evidence; no account or spread was tested by PropRadar.

restrictiveRules.rule: Terms clause 6.9: Moneta Funded "may place any Payout request on hold" for trading, risk, account-association, compliance or abuse reviews and, if it determines "in its sole discretion" that Prohibited Conduct occurred, "may delay, reduce, deduct from, refuse, cancel, or void any Payout request, whether pending or future". Prohibited Conduct (clause 5.2) includes "any activity that we determine, in our sole discretion, constitutes abusive trading or provides an unfair advantage", "one-sided betting" (positions "without proper market analysis") and behaviour "not reproducible or sustainable in real markets". Clause 5.3 allows immediate termination without refund.
restrictiveRules.impact: A pending or future payout can be reduced or cancelled on the firm's own assessment, including under prohibitions without objective thresholds; the account can also be closed without a fee refund.

restrictiveRules.rule: Terms clause 5.2(f) prohibits "Accessing multiple accounts from the same IP address or allowing an account to be used from multiple IP addresses". Breach of clause 5.2 allows termination without refund (5.3) and refusal or voiding of payouts (6.9). The help-centre list of prohibited methods does not mention this IP rule.
restrictiveRules.impact: Logging in from more than one IP address, or running two accounts from one IP (for example a shared household connection), can lead to account termination and cancelled payouts.

restrictiveRules.rule: The help centre lists Martingale, reverse trading, high-frequency trading, order spamming, hedging and grid trading, latency arbitrage, tick scalping, demo-environment exploitation and account sharing as prohibited, and third-party or commercial EAs and signal services are not permitted (terms 5.2(q): no EA "that is not developed by you"); EAs are not allowed on the Sprint Challenge. "Use of any prohibited strategies will result in immediate account termination"; unauthorised EA use "may be subject to profit adjustment or account action".
restrictiveRules.impact: Using a bought or third-party EA, grid or hedging approach can end the account and remove profits before payout.

restrictiveRules.rule: Instant Funding accounts carry a consistency limit chosen at purchase (15% or 20%): best-day realised P&L divided by total realised P&L in the payout cycle must stay within the limit (terms clause 5.1F). If exceeded, "the Account will not be eligible for a Payout until sufficient additional realised profit has been generated". The rule resets after each payout.
restrictiveRules.impact: A single strong day blocks the payout until enough further profit dilutes it; the cheaper 15% option is stricter.

restrictiveRules.rule: Instant Funding Pro has a Maximum Profit Per Day of 4% of the starting balance, measured from equity at the 22:00 UTC snapshot. Once reached, open trades close automatically, trading is disabled until the next reset, and profit above the cap does not count (terms clause 5.1G: it "may be excluded from eligible Account profit").
restrictiveRules.impact: Gains above 4% in a day are closed out and are not payable.

restrictiveRules.rule: 1-Step Daily payouts are capped per request: $1,000 on a $50K account, $2,000 on $100K and $4,000 on $200K. Terms clause 6.10: eligible profit above the Maximum Payout Per Request "may be eligible for a subsequent Payout request". All positions must be closed before requesting.
restrictiveRules.impact: Profit above the per-request cap stays on the account and remains exposed to the 2% static maximum loss until a later request.

restrictiveRules.program: Funded accounts — floating loss per symbol
restrictiveRules.rule: A floating loss on one symbol of 2% of account size (3% on 2-Step with the 5% daily-loss option and on Instant Funding Pro) closes all open trades, disables trading until the 22:00 UTC reset and moves the account to a 1.5% risk-per-trade-idea limit. Once on that limit, exceeding 1.5% breaches the account with no further warning. The limit can be lifted after 14 days and 20 trades on a separate funded account.
restrictiveRules.impact: A second excursion beyond 1.5% on one trade idea ends the funded account, well inside the published daily and maximum loss limits.

restrictiveRules.rule: Terms clause 5.1J: the Risk Team "may impose an additional Risk Per Trade Idea limit" where activity shows "excessive concentration, repeated risk warnings, unsustainable risk exposure, material risk escalation or other risk-management concerns", and may apply it to all funded accounts of the trader; exceeding a notified limit "may result in the affected Account being breached". The help article states only the affected account is restricted after a floating-loss trigger.
restrictiveRules.impact: A tighter per-trade risk limit can be applied on the firm's assessment, across all of a trader's funded accounts, and breaking it ends the account.

restrictiveRules.rule: Opening or closing a trade (including TP/SL triggers) is barred from 5 minutes before to 5 minutes after a scheduled high-impact event on instruments tied to the affected currency; trades opened at least 2 hours earlier may close in the window. "Net profits generated from trades that violate this rule may be subject to deduction"; repeated attempts "may result in account restriction or violation". Sprint also bars gap, market-open and market-close trading.
restrictiveRules.impact: Profit from trades in the news window can be deducted from the payout; repeated cases can end the account.

restrictiveRules.rule: The comparison page and the news-trading article say news trading is allowed on Instant Funding Pro and Phoenix ("the restrictions below do not apply"), but the prohibited-methods article states "Moneta Funded does not allow traders to engage in news trading across all accounts (evaluation & funded)" without exception, and terms clause 5.2(h) lists news trading as Prohibited Conduct with no programme carve-out.

restrictiveRules.program: Instant Funding, Instant Funding Pro — payout
restrictiveRules.rule: The funded account uses a trailing maximum loss (5% on Instant Funding bought from 2 July 2026, 6% before; 8% on Instant Funding Pro). For accounts bought after 21 September 2026 it locks at the initial balance "at payout approval" and does not reset; "Withdrawing all available profit may leave no buffer and can cause the account to be breached immediately".
restrictiveRules.impact: Withdrawing the full profit can end the account on approval, so part of each payout effectively has to be left as buffer.

restrictiveRules.rule: Payouts require 3 profitable days of at least 0.5% each (2-Step funded stage; Phoenix, together with a 14-day interval from the first trade). Days count only if Min(midnight balance, midnight equity) minus previous-day balance meets the threshold (terms 5.1E).

restrictiveRules.rule: Terms clause 6.12: "Following successful payment of the applicable Sprint Payout, the Sprint Account will be permanently closed. The homepage describes a two-phase evaluation ('The Test' and 'The Confirmation') with funding up to $200,000, leverage up to 1:100 and no time limit, but shows no programme names, sizes or prices, and the FAQ blocks automated reading. set.auditSummary: Deep rules audit on 17 November 2026 using OFP's official help centre and terms, expanding the October program-price review. Daily drawdown is recalculated at GMT+2 (with DST) from previous-day closing equity, so an intraday breach can terminate a challenge even after profits made the prior day. A separate maximum 1% floating loss rule is described as 'soft': breach resets account balance rather than directly terminating the account. OFP reserves the right to withhold reward eligibility for its Inconsistency Score and prohibits delayed-feed/arbitrage exploitation, cross-account hedging, AI/HFT or mass-entry systems and some news-gap strategies. Its FAQ advertises typical processing of 2–3 business days; it describes bank/USDC for amounts under $500 and Rise above $500 with a $50 fee. None of those payment statements was confirmed by independent transfer records. The existing October Trustpilot breach/fake-review notice remains disclosed. No spread, slippage or firsthand withdrawal test was conducted.

set.auditSummary: Detailed official help-centre audit on 17 November 2026. A reward request requires 14 days since the previous payout (or seven with a paid weekly add-on; first cycle starts with first trade), no open trades, no pending/limit orders, a within-cap consistency ratio, and at least $100 after the profit split. Trading goes to view-only while the request is processed. A separate official article explains that a funded breach, including a drawdown or unauthorized automation discovered at payout review, permanently closes the account and voids simulated gains including gains accrued before the breach. The May 2026 multiple-IP policy permits different devices/addresses but expects geographical IP-region consistency: changes can prompt travel evidence, a passport stamp or live location video; this must not be misreported as a universal VPN/VPS ban. The 10 November eligibility guide lists UAE and several other restricted countries and explicitly cautions that successful checkout does not establish the legal right to receive services. Source dates and model-specific thresholds are given so users can verify before purchase. The earlier Trustpilot rating-withheld notice and firm-reported $1M+ payout counter remain separately labeled; neither proves payment verification. PropRadar's commercial relationship has no role in this assessment, and no firsthand payout/spread test occurred.

restrictiveRules.rule: Best Day Rule on the funded stage: the best day's profit must be at most 50% of total profit from profitable days to be eligible for a payout (Flash also applies 50% during the evaluation). 'This rule doesn't breach your account'; the ratio resets after each processed payout. Older purchases keep earlier caps.

restrictiveRules.rule: On Instant accounts the Best Day Profit Ratio cap is 'fixed at 15%' (previously 20%); the ratio must be at or below the cap to be eligible for a payout.
restrictiveRules.impact: Any single strong day delays the payout until total profit is about seven times that day.

restrictiveRules.rule: Max Exposure Rule: a trade idea's combined floating loss must not exceed 1% of equity on Instant accounts. 'Reaching the 1% limit is a hard breach', deactivating the account 'from the first occurrence'.
restrictiveRules.impact: A single trade idea with more than 1% floating loss ends the Instant account.

restrictiveRules.program: Flash, Core, Value (challenges bought on or after 13 October 2026)
restrictiveRules.rule: Max Exposure Rule: combined floating loss on a trade idea must not exceed 2% of equity (100k and 200k accounts) or 3% (smaller accounts). The first two breaches are warnings; the third is a hard breach that deactivates the account. Breaches are counted per account.
restrictiveRules.impact: A third exposure breach ends the account, including in the funded stage.

restrictiveRules.rule: At least one trade is required every 60 days in the evaluation and every 30 days in the funded stage; otherwise 'the funded account will be closed, with no eligibility for refunds or payout bonuses'.
restrictiveRules.impact: A funded account left untraded for 30 days is closed.

restrictiveRules.rule: The prohibited-practices article lists practices without numeric thresholds (e.g. 'Tick Scalping' with 'Ultra-short holding times', 'One-Sided Bets', unauthorised copy trading, cross-account hedging) and states 'Violations may result in trading restrictions, cancellation of payouts, suspension of the account, or termination of the Trader Agreement'; the firm keeps 'the sole and final right to determine' whether a practice is prohibited.
restrictiveRules.impact: Payouts can be cancelled on the firm's own assessment of practices that are not defined by figures.

restrictiveRules.rule: News trading is permitted, but trades in the News Volatility Period (5 minutes before to 5 minutes after red high-impact news) that appear to exploit price spikes may be reviewed, and repeated activity focused on that window 'may be deemed a breach'; listed actions 'including but not limited to' a warning, suspension, a challenge restart or account termination.
restrictiveRules.impact: Profitable news trades can lead to a review and, if repeated, to termination at the firm's assessment.

restrictiveRules.rule: Fully automated EAs are prohibited and any EA or trading assistant needs prior approval. A consistent pattern of order clustering, frequent trading without stop loss, ultra-short trades or 14+ hours of daily trading 'may result in the account being reviewed or breached'; single incidents are not automatically a breach.
restrictiveRules.impact: The account can be breached on a pattern assessment without a numeric threshold.

restrictiveRules.rule: Trading from several devices and IPs is allowed, but the IP region 'should remain consistent'; on a detected region change the team may request 'an airline ticket, passport stamp, or live video confirmation of your location'. Devices or IPs tied to another user's account or to suspicious activity may lead to termination.
restrictiveRules.impact: A change of location can add a verification step before the account or payout proceeds.

set.verdict: OneUp Trader operates established futures evaluations but its funded rulebook restricts any trading activity lasting less than 10 seconds, prohibits specific major-news trading and requires weekly activity compared with evaluation. A fast stop-loss or take-profit is a practical concern, but the official page does not state an SL/TP exemption or exception. Standard and Pro evaluations have different minimum days; Express is requalification for a former funded trader, not a new instant purchase. Score reduced from 72 to 70 for funded execution restrictions, not integrity allegations.
set.auditSummary: 18 November 2026 official OneUp rules check: standard evaluation requires ten trading days; Pro requires five and Express requalification three, with an unusual consistency test in which the next three best days combined must represent at least 80% of the best day. Funding uses real-time trailing loss on account equity until its floor locks at initial capital. The funded trader rules ban trades with duration under ten seconds, some major-news executions, and require weekly trades to be at least 50% of the evaluation weekly average; monitoring over the first 90 days may flag negative 15-day periods. Express is not general-purpose instant funding. Because these policies can conflict with ordinary fast exits and change strategy requirements after passing, editorial score lowered two points to 70. No inference of improper nonpayment.

set.auditSummary: Deep audit (17 November 2026) against RebelsFunding's official all-rules page (version 3.2, updated 11 November), terms and FAQ. Evaluation services are attributed to Slovakia-based RIFM, s.r.o.; any RCF collaboration needs a separately approved contract involving RIFM and FRCSM, s.r.o. The Gold program requires an evaluation 10% profit target and eight independent real trades, has no evaluation daily loss ceiling but 6% overall fixed drawdown, and starts at a 75% reward share with no evaluation-fee refund. RCF is still simulated and introduces a 4% daily loss threshold, a 1.5% maximum risk per trade idea and restrictions around high-impact news. The first reward request cannot precede 14 calendar days after the first RCF trade, must be at least $50 and requires closed positions; passing does not automatically create an entitlement. The terms prohibit paid-program EAs and arbitrage/split-trade rule evasion. Website program claims were checked, but no independent deposit receipt, trade-execution/slippage study or customer-level payout transfer was authenticated; the 90% advertised maximum is conditional.

set.auditSummary: The official challenge agreement (17 November 2026 review) offers a more useful risk picture than the sales homepage alone. Section 7.4 prohibits different strategies in evaluation versus funded simulation and cross-account hedging; section 7.5 leaves classification of prohibited trading to the firm's discretion. Section 9 conditions access on identity verification and cites an 80% trader share, contrasting with the 'up to 90%' homepage claim (upgrades or conditions were not independently established). Section 10 lists restricted jurisdictions including Japan, Pakistan, Vietnam, Myanmar, Afghanistan and others; this is published company eligibility, not a legal opinion or proof that a checkout accepts another country. set.verdict: The Concept Trading advertises profit sharing up to 90%, but its published default for every model is 50%; 90% needs top-level progression or the optional Lock Rule, which sacrifices further scaling. set.auditSummary: PropRadar's 17 November 2026 desk audit read the official current FAQ, All Rules and Terms for program-level catches. The firm's standard profit-share arrangement begins at 50% on every model; 90% is offered at a top program level or through the 90% Lock Rule. Lock activation is unavailable on Foundation and Intern accounts, requires first reaching the chosen scaling milestone and receiving its normal split, and prevents further account scaling after election. Once on Level 1 or higher, rewards are triggered by a scaling target; otherwise the FAQ permits one withdrawal per month, rising to weekly at the highest level or with the Lock Rule. Most importantly, the official FAQ requires a profit-sharing invoice within 30 days after hitting the scaling target or the entitlement is forfeited; a six-week/42-day inactivity period also terminates the account. The FAQ excludes Iran, North Korea and US-sanctioned jurisdictions and says US residents cannot use Metaquotes platforms, though other platforms are accepted. It describes static drawdowns varying by plan, not a single universal percentage. These rules and the firm's public financial-service authorisation claims have not been independently verified via a regulator in this pass; no hands-on execution, spread comparison or verified bank payout exists.

restrictiveRules.rule: The terms ban "other conduct which in the sole discretion of the Company, represents uncommercial activity, is intended to game the market, or otherwise is not a viable trading strategy" (Trading Rule 19). The prohibited-practices FAQ adds unquantified items such as "one-sided bets", "bulk trading, is when multiple trades are open simultaneously", position sizes "substantially larger or smaller than your typical trading activity", "disproportionate concentrated exposure" and "speculative position-taking that resembles gambling". On a breach the FAQ states: "Any refund or profit will not be processed, and you will be permanently banned." (prohibited-trading-practices FAQ)
restrictiveRules.impact: Earned profit can be withheld and the trader banned on criteria with no published threshold, assessed at the firm's sole discretion; the rules apply to evaluation and funded accounts.

restrictiveRules.rule: Section 3.2: if the Company requests an interview, scheduling and conducting it "must take place within five (5) business days from the date of the request." Failure "will result in the denial of any pending payouts, immediate cancellation of all associated accounts, and termination of the collaboration." The verification process may be conducted "at any time on our sole discretion."
restrictiveRules.impact: A trader who is unavailable for five business days after an interview request (travel, illness) loses pending payouts and every linked account.

restrictiveRules.rule: Section 10.1 (item 11) allows termination for "any defamatory, disparaging, or harmful statements about the Company, its employees, or the Services on any public platform, including but not limited to social media networks, public groups, forums, or review sites", including publishing support tickets or chats. It is "a fundamental breach": accounts terminated "without any refund of fees paid" and "any accrued profits or Reward Balance shall be immediately forfeited."
restrictiveRules.impact: A negative public review or a posted support exchange can cost the trader accrued profits; 'disparaging' and 'harmful' are not defined.

restrictiveRules.rule: Section 7.6: the Company "reserves the right, at its sole and absolute discretion, to establish a maximum payout amount permitted per single transaction". Above that unpublished Payout Threshold, "the approved payout amount shall be disbursed in consecutive weekly installments of $10,000" until paid in full. The threshold is not stated and may change without notice.
restrictiveRules.impact: A large approved payout can be spread over several weeks at $10,000 per week; the trader cannot know in advance from what amount this applies.

restrictiveRules.program: All programmes — VPN and geographic restrictions

Section 1.10: if this or residence in a forbidden/sanctioned territory is discovered "at any stage (including during or after the KYC process)", the account can be closed immediately. Section 1.11: no refund of fees and "Any accrued balance of profits or rewards shall be canceled and forfeited."
restrictiveRules.impact: Using a VPN that masks location, or later being found resident in a restricted country, can void all accrued profits even after KYC.

restrictiveRules.program: All programmes — copy trading and third-party EAs
restrictiveRules.rule: Prohibited: "Trade coordination or copy trading with other traders or accounts", an "EA from a third party, where other traders have the same trades open", "Using an EA from a provider where the trader does not own the source code", and EAs generating "an excessive number of server requests". Consequence: "Any refund or profit will not be processed, and you will be permanently banned."
restrictiveRules.impact: A commercial EA bought without its source code is enough to lose profits, even if no other trader uses it.

restrictiveRules.rule: Prohibited: "High-frequency trading, in which the majority of trade durations span is measured within a few seconds or less" and "Tick Scalping". No minimum duration in seconds is published. Consequence: profit not processed and permanent ban.
restrictiveRules.impact: Scalpers cannot tell how short is too short; the threshold ('a few seconds') is not defined.

set.auditSummary: Official-source review dated 19 November 2026. The homepage sells four futures programmes in 25K to 150K sizes: Elite Daily (one phase, 6% target, one-time list price $178 to $549, daily payouts), Elite Access ($39 evaluation per the help centre plus a $139 to $359 activation fee), Instant Sim Funded ($419 to $939) and Ignite ($218 to $799, copy trading across up to 10 same-size accounts). All use end-of-day trailing drawdowns that lock at $100 above the starting balance. The help centre sets a 15% (Ignite), 20% (Instant), 25% (Elite) or 40% (Elite Access funded, Elite Daily evaluation) best-day consistency rule, payout caps per request and minimum payouts of $250 to $500. Bots and EAs are banned, trades under 10 seconds can lose their profits, VPN use is prohibited, and a news window of 2 minutes applies on funded Elite accounts. After three payouts (five on Elite Daily) a risk review may move the trader to one live account and close the sim accounts. The terms (Top One Futures, LLC, Cheyenne, Wyoming) add that multiple emails are a violation, that either party may cancel 'at any time for any reason', that there are no refunds, and name no governing law or country list. Payout evidence and the broker relationship were not verified.

set.auditSummary: Official-source review dated 19 November 2026. The pricing pages, rules page, June 2026 Terms and help-centre articles were read. Challenges: 1-Step FLASH ($64 to $1,079 list, 10% target, 4% daily, 7% trailing drawdown, 3% funded daily profit cap), 2-Step PRO V2 ($69 to $1,398, 8% then 5%, 9% static, payouts capped at 6% or $15,000 per request), 2-Step Plus ($78 to $998, 10% then 5%, 8% static, five 0.5% profitable days before each payout) and NOVA ($1 to start plus an activation fee after passing). Sim-funded accounts: Instant Funding ($135 to $2,537, 6% trailing, 15% consistency, split 60% rising to 90%, 30-day payouts, possible video interview before a withdrawal), Instant Prime ($94 to $1,776, 5% trailing, ESS 20%, split 80% to 100%) and a limited-time Magnum ($3,495 for $500K, $5,995 for $1M, 4% trailing, $25,000 per rolling 30 days). Across programmes the terms state a VPN ban, a 5-minute minimum hold for profitable trades, a 30-day inactivity breach, funded lot-exposure caps, mandatory stop losses on several accounts, an EA ban with forfeiture of gains, and a sole-discretion clause on risk practices. Payouts run every 14 days on most accounts through Rise with a 2% fee. The Terms name Top One Trader, LLC; the footer names Top One Trader Ltd in Anjouan with a firm-stated licence that PropRadar has not verified. Trustpilot withholds the rating after a guideline breach.
set.verdict: Top One Trader sells FLASH, 2-Step PRO V2, 2-Step Plus and NOVA challenges plus Instant Funding, Instant Prime and Magnum sim-funded accounts. The fine print adds a 5-minute hold rule, a VPN ban, $25,000 rolling payout caps, split ladders starting at 60% or 80%, funded lot caps and an EA ban. Payout evidence is third-party only and the Anjouan licence is unverified.

restrictiveRules.rule: 'The use of VPNs is strictly prohibited'; VPS allowed only with a static IP and advance notice of changes. 'Using different IP addresses to access a single account may raise flags and be considered a violation.' 'Any serious violations of this IP policy will result in a breach of your account and forfeiture of any profits.' The Terms also prohibit 'Using multiple ip addresses on your account'.
restrictiveRules.impact: Trading through a VPN or from changing IPs can end the account and cancel profits.

restrictiveRules.program: All programmes — challenge and simulated funded accounts
restrictiveRules.rule: 'All profitable trades must be held for at least 5 full minutes before they are closed.' On funded accounts 'Profits from non-compliant trades will be deducted' with a formal warning; repeated violations after the warning may lead to termination. In a challenge, the trader may have to retake it.
restrictiveRules.impact: Profits on winning trades closed within 5 minutes are removed from the payout; repeat cases can end the account.

restrictiveRules.rule: It is 'prohibited to execute or close any trade within the window of 5 minutes before and 5 minutes after' a high-impact news event on funded accounts. First violation is a soft breach: 'Any gains made from such trades will be deducted'; repeated violations can lead to a hard breach or termination.
restrictiveRules.impact: News-window profits are removed from the payout.

restrictiveRules.program: Instant Funding (15%) and Instant Prime Exclusive (ESS 20%)
restrictiveRules.rule: Instant Funding: consistency score 'Must remain at 15% or below' (accounts bought on or after 14 October 2025). Instant Prime: ESS 'Must be met before becoming eligible for a payout' (20% on the pricing table).
restrictiveRules.impact: Payouts are blocked until the best-day share falls under the threshold.

restrictiveRules.rule: ESS must be at or below 20%: 'If ESS exceeds the threshold, the payout is not eligible and the trader must continue trading.'
restrictiveRules.impact: Payout delayed until profits are spread across more days.

restrictiveRules.rule: 'a maximum of $25,000 in net profits and total withdrawals within any rolling thirty (30) day period', across all funded accounts of the same trader; 'any excess profits may be deducted from the Trader's account balance(s).' Minimum withdrawal 2% of the initial balance.
restrictiveRules.impact: Profits above $25,000 per rolling 30 days can be removed rather than carried over.

restrictiveRules.rule: 'Each payout request is limited to 6% of the account size', with a $15,000 maximum per request; a request needs at least 3% profit and 'at least 3 profitable trading days' (each at least 0.5% of the starting balance).
restrictiveRules.impact: Profits above 6% of the account (or $15,000) wait for later cycles.

restrictiveRules.program: Instant Funding / Instant Prime — funded account
restrictiveRules.rule: The funded account carries a maximum trailing drawdown (6% of initial balance on Instant Funding, 5% on Instant Prime), a hard breach; after a payout the 'maximum drawdown will be locked at your initial balance'.
restrictiveRules.impact: Until the first payout, the loss floor rises with equity highs, so giving back open gains can breach the account.

restrictiveRules.rule: The NOVA funded stage lists a 5% maximum trailing drawdown; 'After a payout, the drawdown will lock at the starting balance.'
restrictiveRules.impact: Until the first payout the loss floor trails equity highs.

restrictiveRules.rule: Soft breaches (trade without a stop loss, more than 2% open loss per symbol or 2.5% on all open trades, exceeding max lots on funded accounts, weekend holding on Instant) close the trades; Instant Funding allows 10 soft breaches, 'after which it becomes a hard breach' (Instant Prime: 5). Hard breach: 'your account will be closed and any gains forfeited.'
restrictiveRules.impact: Repeated risk-limit hits accumulate toward account closure.

restrictiveRules.rule: Profit split 'rises from 80% (first payout) to 90% (second) to 100% (third and later)'; 100% from the start only with a paid add-on. The pricing card shows 'up to 100%'.
restrictiveRules.impact: The first two payouts are paid at a lower split than the headline figure.

restrictiveRules.rule: The Terms list as prohibited 'Trading in any way that Top One Trader deems, in its sole discretion, to be outside of acceptable risk practices' (participation 'will be terminated') and state 'Any type of over-leveraging or gambling behavior may result in deduction of profits or termination of a trader's account.'
restrictiveRules.impact: Profits can be deducted or the account closed on a risk assessment the firm makes at its sole discretion.

restrictiveRules.rule: 'Not placing a trade at least once every 30 days' is a hard breach: the account is closed and any gains forfeited.
restrictiveRules.impact: An account idle for 30 days is closed.

restrictiveRules.program: All programmes — Terms of Use, prohibited uses (EAs, HFT, signals)
restrictiveRules.rule: The Terms state 'Using any type of commercially available EA with automated trading strategies is strictly forbidden' and 'Masking of EAs is forbidden', with 'the immediate closing of your account and the forfeiture of any gains'; for HFT or tick scalping the Company 'will deduct any gains produced from trades violating this policy'; following signal programs where multiple traders execute the same trades is prohibited. Help articles add that EAs are not permitted on funded 2-Step PRO V2, 2-Step Plus, Instant Funding and Magnum accounts.
restrictiveRules.impact: Running an off-the-shelf EA can end the account with its gains; HFT-style profits are removed from the payout.

restrictiveRules.rule: Funded FLASH accounts have a 3% daily profit cap: profit above it is voided, which is 'not a breach'. The comparison article also lists a '$25k/month max payout'.
restrictiveRules.impact: Profit above 3% of the account in one day does not count toward the payout.

restrictiveRules.rule: A trader may keep a maximum of '$25,000 in net profits and total withdrawals within any thirty (30) day period' across all accounts; profits above that are deducted from the trading balance.
restrictiveRules.impact: Profits above $25,000 per 30 days can be removed rather than carried over.

restrictiveRules.rule: Payouts are capped at $25,000 per customer per rolling 30 days, and a minimum of $10,000 profit (2% of the $500K balance) is required before a withdrawal.
restrictiveRules.impact: On a $500K account, monthly withdrawals cannot exceed $25,000 whatever the profit.

restrictiveRules.rule: A payout cap applies per payout cycle ('the remaining balance stays on the account and can be withdrawn in future payout cycles'); funded max profit is 5% per day, treated as a soft breach.
restrictiveRules.impact: Large profits are paid out over several cycles, and a day above 5% profit counts as a soft breach.

restrictiveRules.rule: '60% on your first payout, rising by 10% per payout', reaching 90% from the fourth payout; the homepage pricing card shows a 90% split.
restrictiveRules.impact: The first three payouts are paid at 60%, 70% and 80% instead of the headline 90%.

restrictiveRules.rule: Profit split is 80% on the first payout, 90% on the second and 100% from the third; 100% from the first payout only with a paid add-on.
restrictiveRules.impact: The first two payouts are paid below the headline split.

restrictiveRules.rule: Top One Trader 'may require a video interview' before processing a withdrawal; it must be completed within one week of the request, or 'the withdrawal may be denied'. Payouts also require a 15% consistency score and follow a 30-day cycle.
restrictiveRules.impact: A payout can be refused if the interview is not completed within a week.

restrictiveRules.rule: The 7% maximum drawdown is trailing and a hard breach on challenge and funded accounts; it locks at the starting balance when a payout is requested (the comparison article adds: or after a 7% gain).
restrictiveRules.impact: Until the lock, the loss floor rises with gains, so giving back profits can breach the funded account.

restrictiveRules.rule: Maximum trailing drawdown of 4% of initial balance ($20,000), a hard breach; it trails the closing balance until a +4% gain, then locks at the starting balance.
restrictiveRules.impact: Until the account is 4% up, the loss floor rises with each new closing-balance high.

restrictiveRules.program: 1-Step FLASH and 2-Step PRO V2 — profitable days
restrictiveRules.rule: FLASH requires 'at least 3 profitable trading days' to advance; 2-Step PRO V2 requires 3 profitable days per phase, each at least 0.5%.
restrictiveRules.impact: Hitting the target in fewer profitable days does not pass the phase.

restrictiveRules.rule: Five separate days closing with at least 0.5% net profit are required to finish a phase or to request a payout.
restrictiveRules.impact: A payout request waits until five qualifying profitable days are recorded.

restrictiveRules.program: 2-Step PRO V2, 2-Step Plus, NOVA, Instant Funding, Magnum — funded news
restrictiveRules.rule: News trading is allowed in the challenge phases but not on funded 2-Step PRO V2, 2-Step Plus and NOVA accounts; it is 'Not allowed' on Instant Funding (Instant Prime: allowed with an add-on); on Magnum trading is blocked within 5 minutes either side of high-impact news unless an add-on is bought. The pages read do not state a payout consequence for these programmes.
restrictiveRules.impact: Funded traders must stay out of high-impact news windows.

restrictiveRules.program: Instant Funding / Instant Prime and Magnum — weekend
restrictiveRules.rule: Weekend holding is 'Not allowed' on Instant Funding unless the weekend holding add-on is bought (a soft breach otherwise); the homepage FAQ says the add-on must be purchased on Instant Funding and Prime accounts; Magnum: not allowed by default, add-on available.
restrictiveRules.impact: Positions must be closed before the weekend unless a paid add-on is bought.

restrictiveRules.program: All programmes — funded lot exposure, stop loss and Equity Shield
restrictiveRules.rule: Simulated funded accounts have a hard-enforced maximum lot exposure (1 lot on $5k, 2 on $10k, 5 on $25k, 10 on $50k, 20 on $100k and above): 'if your total open lots exceed the limit, all open trades are closed (soft breach)'. FLASH, Instant and Magnum also require a stop loss on every trade unless an add-on is bought, and Equity Shield closes trades when open losses exceed 2% on one symbol or 2.5% in total.
restrictiveRules.impact: Positions above the lot cap or without a stop loss are closed automatically.

restrictiveRules.program: 2-Step PRO V2, 2-Step Plus, Magnum — soft-breach limits
restrictiveRules.rule: 2-Step PRO V2 allows a 'Maximum of 8' soft breaches per account: 'Once the limit is reached, the account may be breached or restricted.' 2-Step Plus lists a soft-breach limit of 4 (with a 1% Equity Shield) and Magnum a maximum of 5; the Magnum article does not say what happens after the fifth.
restrictiveRules.impact: Repeated Equity Shield, lot or stop-loss hits can lead to the account being breached at the firm's discretion.

set.verdict: Topstep remains an active futures evaluation service. Standard Trading Combine and Express Funded use an end-of-day trailing maximum-loss limit, but the Express Funded nominal account size is buying power: its real starting balance is zero. The floor locks at zero and a first payout sets it to zero regardless of prior position. A separate 40% consistency route applies only to the selected XFA payout path. These are documented rules; PropRadar score 82/100 after a modest deduction for complexity and withdrawal gates.
set.auditSummary: 18 November 2026 official Topstep September 2026 help-center audit. Trading Combine sizes $50K, $100K, $150K have maximum loss limits of $2,000, $3,000, $4,500, each trailing end-of-day balance but enforced against realtime unrealized net P/L intraday; the floor eventually locks at starting size. Evaluation has a 55% profit concentration target, whereas its Express Funded Account starts at $0 despite nominal $50K–$150K buying power; its MLL trails from negative amounts to a permanent $0 floor, and the first reward resets the MLL to zero. XFA Standard and Consistency payout routes differ; Consistency requires best day ≤40% of window profit and at least three trading days; payouts reset the window. A daily loss limit may be selected at checkout and changes some parameters. No legal incident added or independent bank-level examination; editor score 84 to 82 for complexity, not proof of unfair denial.

restrictiveRules.rule: MLL trails end-of-day balance and is recalculated at daily close, but an intraday unrealized equity touch triggers liquidation. Standard Combine profit-day concentration is limited to 55% of its target.
restrictiveRules.impact: Profitable open positions that reverse can breach a threshold set at the previous EOD; a single oversized winning day delays passing.

restrictiveRules.rule: Despite a nominal $50K–$150K buying-power label, the XFA starts at $0. MLL rises from a negative floor, locks at $0 and is set to $0 after first payout; on the optional Consistency payout path, best day ≤40% and at least 3 trading days.
restrictiveRules.impact: A payout can reduce remaining loss cushion, and payout eligibility differs between Standard and Consistency paths.

restrictiveRules.program: Topstep Trading Combine and XFA — daily loss options
restrictiveRules.rule: Daily Loss Limit is not necessarily universal: checkout can add DLL and change a funded payout cap; self-set personal loss controls are distinct from mandatory MLL.
restrictiveRules.impact: Do not present an optional daily lockout as a compulsory hard breach for every Topstep programme.

restrictiveRules.rule: Each Express Funded Account payout is limited to "50% of your account balance up to the cap", with caps from $2,000 to $6,000 depending on account size and payout path. "Minimum Payout: $125." Live Funded Account payouts are not capped.
restrictiveRules.impact: Only part of the accumulated profit can be withdrawn per request on the simulated funded account; the rest stays exposed to the Maximum Loss Limit.

restrictiveRules.program: Express Funded Account — Standard payout path
restrictiveRules.rule: A Standard payout requires "5 winning days of $150+ Net P&L" (not necessarily consecutive); after each payout "your 5-day count restarts". At least $0.01 must have been earned since the last payout (first payout exempt).
restrictiveRules.impact: Each payout needs a new set of five qualifying days, so profits made in fewer, larger days wait longer.

restrictiveRules.program: Trading Combine, Express Funded and Live — prohibited conduct
restrictiveRules.rule: Section 27 bans conduct that "knowingly or unknowingly circumvents targets and rules", "Taking advantage of the simulated environment", and anything that "is intended to game the market, is not a viable trading strategy"; section 8 treats "substantially (i) larger position sizes" or "(ii) a smaller or larger number of positions compared to your other trades" as failing risk standards. Topstep may "remove any Simulated Account profits, delete a trading day, reset an Account, or ban a User"; where profits were gained through the simulated environment after graduating, "you will not be entitled to receive any withdrawals from any other account maintained with Topstep", "all of which will be forfeited and closed immediately." The help centre adds "Delay or denial of a Payout request", decided "case-by-case based on severity and history."
restrictiveRules.impact: Profits and withdrawals on every Topstep account can be removed for conduct the firm classifies as prohibited under undefined standards, including unknowing circumvention.

restrictiveRules.program: All accounts — VPN, proxy and remote access
restrictiveRules.rule: Section 28: "Using any VPN, VPS, proxy (including residential), or other service masking your IP address or location on Accounts is strictly prohibited, and violations may result in account termination and forfeiture of profits"; location spoofing apps and remote access tools are also banned.
restrictiveRules.impact: Trading through a VPS or VPN (common for automated setups) can cost the account and its profits.

restrictiveRules.program: All accounts — coordinated trading and cross-account hedging
restrictiveRules.rule: Prohibited: "performing trades in concert with others (including unconnected accounts or third parties)", "holding opposite positions across multiple accounts simultaneously", "repeatedly hitting the Maximum Loss Limit in one account and switching to another" (account stacking), and trading on behalf of others. Listed consequences include "Delay or denial of a Payout request" and "Permanent account closure".
restrictiveRules.impact: Following the same signals as other traders, or hedging between one's own accounts, can lead to payout denial or closure.

restrictiveRules.program: Express Funded Account — live restricted jurisdictions
restrictiveRules.rule: Section 30: in Live Restricted Jurisdictions (where Topstep "does not maintain an active relationship with a futures commission merchant partner who accepts live traders"), "any such Express Funded Account will operate exclusively in a simulated trading environment" and "Restricted Participants will not migrate from an Express Funded Account to a Live Funded Account, regardless of trading performance".
restrictiveRules.impact: Traders in those countries stay on the capped simulated payout path permanently; the uncapped Live Funded payouts are not available to them.

restrictiveRules.rule: Section 9: "If you do not activate the Trading Combine® within 30 calendar days of the date on which it was made available to you, your access to it will be suspended"; it must be renewed within 6 months of the suspension, "otherwise we will terminate the provision of the Services" without a fee refund.
restrictiveRules.impact: A Combine bought but not started within 30 days is suspended and can be lost after six months.

restrictiveRules.rule: Trading Rules are "subject to change by Topstep in its sole and absolute discretion from time to time" and account parameters "remain subject to adjustment and change from time to time, without notice" (sections 27 and 9). Changes to the Terms themselves require notice.
restrictiveRules.impact: Rules and parameters on an existing account can change without notice; the terms do not protect accounts already bought.

set.auditSummary: 18 November 2026: reconciled current programme comparison against contractual Program Terms. set.auditSummary: Official-source review dated 19 November 2026. TradeXProp's homepage, pricing pages, forex and crypto FAQs, help-desk rules articles and Terms of Use (last modified 16 July 2025) were read. Forex X 1-Step ($45 to $3,755) has a 10% target and 6% static drawdown; X 2-Step ($35 to $2,465) has 8% then 5% targets and an 8% static drawdown, both with a 5% daily loss, no time limit and an 80% split. Crypto X-1 Step ($45 to $2,150) and X-2 Step ($35 to $2,000) trade on DXtrade with 9% or 6%/9% targets, static 6% or 9% drawdowns and a 3% daily cap in both directions; the pricing table shows a 90% split while the crypto help article says up to 80%. Instant Funded X ($200 to $5,000) has no target and a trailing drawdown given as 8% on the homepage but 5% on its own page. The forex rules state a 45% best-day consistency limit for evaluation (the target is raised otherwise) and for each funded payout, no trades within 3 minutes of news, no strategy change between evaluation and funded, and a breach after 30 days without trading. The Terms prohibit copy trading between accounts the trader does not own, cross-account hedging, third-party pass strategies and undefined 'gambling' or excessive leverage, with account closure and forfeiture of amounts owed as possible consequences. Forex payouts are bi-weekly after the first eligible payout; crypto withdrawals are at most every 30 days; open trades must be closed before a request. The Terms and footer name Prop Account, LLC as provider within a group that includes Forest Park FX LTD; no registration number or address is published. Payout evidence was not independently verified.

Two further unlabelled tables (9% target, 5:1 leverage) are not recorded because the page does not name the program.

set.auditSummary: Deep document review on 17 November 2026 of the official terms last updated 10 November and the current FAQ. Section 17.4 adds a funded-stage Daily PNL Cap: the largest profit day cannot exceed 30% of cumulative account profit for reward eligibility. Program appendices distinguish 20% consistency on Instant Funded from 40% (2-Step evaluation), 50% (1-Step evaluation) and 30% (funded). Withdrawals on the listed WGF models can be requested only on the 16th to the last day of each month (UTC), after at least seven calendar days from the cycle's first trade and any qualifying-day requirement, with at most 50% of accumulated P&L per request and additional absolute caps determined by account size and sequence. For challenge graduates the currently described activation charge is EUR 199; a EUR 99 upfront payment option waives the later fee, but is non-refundable on failure. The No-Consistency add-on applies to a 2-Step challenge evaluation, not to its resulting funded account. The 1-Step EOD trailing drawdown continues rising with higher end-of-day balances, unlike the earlier broad claim that every 1-Step drawdown locks to starting capital. These are published company terms, not verified settlements, legal eligibility confirmations or live spread tests. PropRadar's previous payout timing description has been corrected rather than left as a misleading legacy promise.
